account. (4) **Metaculus:** Metaculus's analysis repo has no question or forecast data, so a bot can only be measured by entering it; MiniBench's two-week
rounds are the fastest real test. Prizes are concentrated at the top (Metaculus weighed score-squared and exponential splits to avoid flat payouts).

## 1026. Tradeify allows personal bots — the existing plan can become the automated core once API access exists (S11)

**No trial.** Tradeify's help-centre "Guidelines for traders" (fetched 2026-10-25, "updated over a week ago"): **personal bots are allowed unless they are HFT**.
Conditions: you must prove you are the sole owner; Tradeify may require a live video of you enabling the code on your own PC (so the bot should run on your
machine, not only the droplet); using the same bot at other firms is prohibited; funded payouts need > 50% of trades and > 50% of profit from holds over 10 seconds
(the NKD rule's holds are minutes to hours). Connections: Tradovate, Rithmic or WealthCharts, fixed at purchase (vendor blogs). The binding
constraint stays the one you reported on 10-15: no API order placement until the account reaches the live stage. Until then, staged bracket orders
(§581) are the semi-automated path. For the combined-stack rule, the Tradeify plan is the only scalable automatable piece found so far (prop capital supplies the scale).

## 1027. Screen: free paper-trading competitions with cash prizes — a real lottery-ticket structure, but EV is a few dollars an entry; closed (S11)

**No trial (desk).** Mechanism: free entry plus ranking by ROI means a maximum-variance strategy buys a free lottery ticket with EV = prize pool × P(top).
Current: TradingView "The Leap" ($50k cash for 2026-07-20 → 08-14; paid or trial TradingView account; ≥ 5 trading days; typically
tens of thousands of entrants, so ≈ a few dollars of EV each, and everyone else also plays high-variance); Trading.com monthly (US clients, forex demo, up to $6k;
forex, close to the user's exclusions); GoChamp CME futures (prizes in commission credits, residence-restricted); Moomoo (weekly top-3, 2025 format). Contest rules
on bots are unstated. EV per entry ≈ $1-20 a month and prizes are lumpy, so this is not a stream. Closed.

## 1028. Round-up automation re-check: the stream is narrowing — issuers round at the record-holder level and automated RSA services crowd it (S11)

**No trial (desk).** 2025-26 sources: issuers increasingly apply the round-up "at the record holder level with the transfer agent to prevent arbitrage" (MultiSensor AI,
2026). Street-name brokers may keep the round-up rather than pass it to customers (Impact Biomedical, 2026-09: allocation to customers unexplained). SIFMA asks that
round-ups be eliminated altogether. Commercial "automated RSA signal" services now sell the trade (TradeLabs, OneArbitrage, stocksplitarbitrage). Many RSA
names are OTC or sub-$1, which some API brokers block. With Alpaca out (fractions, §1024), the automatable version is Tradier (fee) plus tastytrade (inconsistent):
≈ $50-150 a month, shrinking. It stays in the stack as a minor piece and is not worth building ahead of anything larger.

## 1029. An automation path for the Tradeify plan exists now: webhook bridges (TradersPost / PickMyTrade) on a Tradovate connection; direct API only later (S11)

**No trial (desk; vendor sources marked).** Tradovate's own API needs a live funded account with ≥ $1,000 equity and a $25/month add-on, and **evaluation accounts are excluded**
(vendor blog). Rithmic's API is approval-only. Tradeify's help centre says TradingView works only through Tradovate. TradersPost and PickMyTrade both advertise
Tradeify automation over Tradovate through webhooks, and they accept a webhook from any source, so the droplet bot that already computes the NKD ticket
could send the bracket order itself, replacing manual staging. Policy (§1026): personal, non-HFT bots allowed; prove sole ownership; possibly a live video of
enabling it on your PC; no use at other firms. **Open points before any build (yours to check or decide):** which connection your account uses (Tradovate is
needed for this path; the connection can't be switched without a new purchase); the bridge's cost (≈ $30-100/month); Tradeify support's written confirmation that a
bridge counts as a personal bot; and any droplet change still needs your confirmation. This is the one path found that makes the scalable stream hands-free.

## 1030. Metaculus bot lead, re-ranked under the automation rule: the strongest automatable stream that needs no capital; Market Pulse adds ≈ $7k a quarter (S11)

**No trial (desk).** Bot-eligible prize pools: seasonal FutureEval ≈ $50-58k × 3 a year, MiniBench ≈ $1k every two weeks (≈ $26k a year), and Market Pulse
≈ $7k a quarter (bots eligible since Q3 2025; bots must update continuously and handle numeric group questions). Total ≈ $200k a year. Prizes are top-weighted:
Q2 2025 ($30k) paid #1 $7,550, #9 $1,731, #20 $465. Scaled to a $58k season, #9 ≈ $3.3k a season. The best single-prompt baseline placed 18th of 173 in Spring 2026,
and top bots are research-plus-ensemble pipelines, so a well-engineered Claude ensemble with AskNews plausibly lands in the top 10-20: ≈ $300-1,000 a month
across all series, and top 3 ≈ $1.6-3.5k. **Fully automatable** (a bot on the droplet), no capital, only API costs (Metaculus grants some credits). It needs your accounts
(Metaculus account, bot account, participation form). Fastest real test: MiniBench's two-week rounds. Combined with the Tradeify plan automated through a bridge (§1029),
it is the most credible automatable path to the user's $2k/month stack.

## 1031. F-family 1 protocol — is a Claude forecaster competitive with top forecasting bots? A blind ForecastBench test on a post-cutoff question set (S11)

**No trial (a skill measurement for the Metaculus lead, §1030). Written before any question is forecast or any resolution is read.** ForecastBench (FRI,
`forecastingresearch/forecastbench-datasets`) question set **2026-07-05** (freeze 2026-06-25; after Claude's training cutoff, so outcomes are unknown).
**Forecasts:** all resolved market questions (Manifold, Metaculus, Polymarket, INFER, as in the tournament fixed-effects file), plus a random 60 of the
dataset questions (seed 1031) at their 7-, 30- and 90-day horizons. Claude forecasts from the question text, background and freeze value only (no web, no
tools beyond reading the file), in batches. Probabilities are saved and hashed before `2026-07-05_resolution_set.json` is opened.
**Scoring, ForecastBench's own method (`src/leaderboard/main.py`):** Brier per forecast minus the published tournament question fixed effect; mean per question type;
shifted so that "Always 0.5" on the same questions scores 0.25; **Brier Index = (1 − √score) × 100** (higher is better). **Read:** compare with the tournament
leaderboard (`leaderboard_tournament.csv`): top-10 Dataset ≈ 63-67, Market ≈ 72-76; superforecaster median 63.5 / 74.5. **Pass for the lead:** both
indices within the top-20 band. Then a Metaculus bot built on Claude is plausibly a top-tier entrant, and the user's accounts are worth asking for. Caveat: one
set (sampling noise), and real bots also use live news, which this test does not.

## 1033. F1 result: a zero-shot Claude forecaster scores at the baseline-LLM tier, not the top — Brier Index 60.3 dataset / 67.5 market; fails the top-20 bar (S11)

**No trial (a measurement).** ForecastBench's method on set 2026-07-05: **dataset 60.3** (180 forecasts; the leaderboard median of 463 entries is 59.8,
Claude Opus 5 baselines 61.5, top-10 63-67, superforecaster median 63.5), **market 67.5** (107; on these same questions, copying the freeze price scores 66.6,
so +0.9 for my adjustments, much like the baselines' +1 over Naive on the leaderboard. Top-10 market scores are 72-76 on other sets). Pooled 62.8. On a single set, the
rescaling against Always 0.5 reduces to the raw Brier, so the numbers sit on the leaderboard scale directly. **Reading:** without a research pipeline,
Claude is a mid-pack forecaster, about where single-model baselines rank. Biggest losses: SpaceX −50% (0.40 vs 0.49, resolved YES), ER seat gains, Mbappé top scorer. Biggest
gains: shading OpenAI's S-1 timing, Hormuz-by-August and Haiti election down. **For the Metaculus lead (§1030):** the prize-relevant ranks need a research-plus-ensemble
pipeline (AskNews, multiple models, aggregation), as the Spring 2026 top bots used. Zero-shot quality alone places it ~rank 50-150 of ~200 eligible bots, i.e.
≈ $0-200 a season. The lead stays parked at its low estimate. Proving a top-tier pipeline needs live news, so the real test is a MiniBench round with your accounts.

## 1040. L-family 27 protocol — premarket laggards: buy the open when a large cap's premarket move trails its beta × QQQ premarket move by > 2% (S11)

**Written before any intraday data is read.** Free data: Yahoo 5-minute bars with pre/post (last ≈ 60 calendar days). Universe: the 100 largest `pack.npz` names by dollar
volume. **Signal at 09:25 ET:** stock premarket return (09:25 last price ÷ prior 16:00 close − 1) minus β × QQQ premarket return (β = 60-session daily beta from
`pack.npz`). **Rule:** residual < −2% and no earnings 8-K in the prior 24 h (from `data/stocks/l23/events.json`) → buy the 09:30 open, sell at the 16:00 close; return minus
QQQ open→close, minus 0.1%. **Statistic:** per-day mean, t on days. This is a discovery read only (≈ 40 sessions); if it carries (mean > 0, t > 1.96), it gets a forward
test, not a sealed window. Automatable through any API broker's open orders. Capital-bound.

## 1041. L-family 27: premarket laggards don't catch up after the open — +0.002% a day, t 0.01; not carried (S11)

**N 1,562 (no trial).** `src/futuresres/stocks/l27_premarket.py`, Yahoo 5-minute bars (2026-07-28 → 10-23, 59 sessions), the 100 most traded `pack.npz` names. With the registered
60-session β vs QQQ: 351 signals on 58 days; open→close minus QQQ minus 0.1% = **+0.002% per day-mean, t +0.01**. Per-trade mean +0.57%, but it is concentrated on
days with few signals; days with many signals (broad selloffs) lose. A first run used β = 1 by mistake (+0.045%, t 0.18), was corrected before reading the result as a
verdict, and is noted here. Closed.

## 1043. §1037 open point closed: TradersPost accepts webhooks from custom code (Python requests POST of JSON), not only TradingView (S11)

**No trial.** TradersPost's docs ("Signal sources → Custom code") show a Python `requests` POST of a JSON body (ticker, action, price) to the strategy's
webhook URL, with a JSON success response and signal ID. The parser is JSON5 (since 2022-12). Stop/target fields for custom JSON are documented on its signal-format page
(to read before any build). So the droplet bot could send the NKD bracket itself. Still open for the user: the account's connection (Tradovate), TradersPost's price, and
Tradeify's written OK.

## 1044. Metaculus bot design note: a market-implied module (options-implied distributions) for finance questions — the one structural edge over LLM bots (S11)

**No trial (desk).** Market Pulse rounds (≈ $7.5k a quarter, bots eligible) ask rolling finance questions: NVIDIA guidance, S&P 500 additions, earnings, VIX maxima over a window.
Seasonal tournaments also carry numeric market questions (e.g. the S&P 500 close on a date). For price and volatility thresholds, the risk-neutral distribution from live
option chains (free, delayed, Yahoo `v7/finance/options`), with a small correction for the variance premium, is close to the best forecast. Most bots reason in text and are
miscalibrated on numeric tails (F1's biggest miss was a −50% SpaceX threshold). This is the only identified structural edge for an automated forecaster, and F2's Bot A tests the
same "use the market's own number" idea on ForecastBench. It would be built only with the user's accounts (§1030).

user's "no liquidity rewards" line, though rebate-free. Blocked. (3) **Borrow-fee arbitrage** (be paid a hard-to-borrow fee through one broker's fully-paid lending while
shorting the same stock at a broker whose borrow rate lags): needs two brokers' daily rates (IBKR's via iborrowdesk is public; payout rates aren't), a margin account, and
capital. The user also rejects IBKR. Blocked. None changes the stack.

## 1052. Screen: tax-lien certificates and Texas tax-deed redemption premiums (S11) — capital-bound, yields bid away; closed

**No trial.** **Lien states** (FL, AZ, AL, LA) run bid-down auctions, many online with uploaded bid lists, so they are partly automatable. Institutional buyers dominate the large auctions,
with yields compressed to roughly 0.25–5% in metro auctions (unsourced industry claim). Arizona's Yavapai County sold 81% of its liens, and the remainder within a week. The national market is ≈ $5bn (NTLA 2024).
Rural higher-yield liens need parcel due diligence (manual) and are capital at par. **Texas tax deeds** pay a 25% or 50% redemption premium on homestead and agricultural property, but
the buyer pays the full bid (thousands per parcel) and bids in person or by county auction. Both are capital-bound. $200 at even 18% is ≈ $3 a month, and scale needs capital in
proportion. This fails the small-start/scale rule. Closed. The stack is unchanged.

## 1053. Synthesis of 2026-10-25's screens (§1045–1052): the binding constraint is "small start × automation", and only three routes survive it (S11)

**No trial.** Every arena screened today failed on one of two walls. **Capital:** the edge is a percentage of one's own money (stale NAVs, borrow arbitrage, lending, tax liens, ERCOT, bond month-end),
so $200 earns dollars a month. **Automation or rules:** the payer bans bots or wants human validation (Gray Swan, HackerOne, poker/chess, DFS), or the pay is one-off and top-heavy (Kaggle and agent
contests). Clearing $2k a month from $100–200 therefore needs someone else's capital or prize money, plus a payer that permits code. Only three routes found so far meet all three conditions:
(1) **Tradeify via the TradersPost webhook bridge** (§1029, §1037, §1043; backtested, not proven), (2) **a Metaculus bot** (FutureEval ≈ $50k a season plus Market Pulse ≈ $7.5k a quarter;
zero-shot is at the baseline tier per F1, so a market-implied module (§1044) is the planned edge; F2 scores 11-09), and (3) **WorldQuant BRAIN** (API automation is common, pay is per-alpha and
unpublished, about a few hundred a month typical). Routes (2) and (3) need the user's own accounts before anything can be measured. The search continues for a fourth route of this shape,
meaning outside capital or prizes, with code allowed and a legitimate US payer.

## 1054. Screen: Tradeify Grand Cup (free simulated futures tournament, $1M pool) and ChartChamps — annual, one entry per person, EV ≈ $50–150 a year; noted, not a route (S11)

**No trial (desk; official T&C at tradeify.co/grandcup-tc and the help-centre guide).** Grand Cup 2 (May 17 – Jun 9, 2026) had a free entry. **Stage 1** was a 5-day qualifier on a $50k sim account with a
$2.5k drawdown, max 1 mini or 10 micros, ranked by ending balance, top 1,000 advancing, with up to 3 resets at $29. **Stage 2** was a 1,024-trader single-elimination bracket of one-day head-to-heads,
1 contract, no drawdown, at least 3 trades held > 10 s each. **All prizes are cash** ($80k per round split among those eliminated: $156 for a round-1 loss up to $200k for the champion, plus
$5k bounties on 24 invited pros), paid by wire with a 1099-MISC. It is open in all 50 US states, and **one contest account per person** (a second means disqualification). The T&C are silent on bots.
**Field:** Grand Cup 1 (2025) drew > 20,000 entrants, so qualifying is roughly the top 5%. The average bracket seat is worth ≈ $1M/1,024 ≈ $977. A free max-variance qualifier attempt,
for example a stop at the $2.5k floor and a trend hold, qualifies perhaps 5–15% of the time, giving **≈ $50–150 EV per year** for one person; each $29 reset is +EV only if P(qualify) > 3%.
It is annual, with no Grand Cup 3 announced. **ChartChamps** (acquired by Tradeify in June 2026) has Elo matches on historical data with no stated cash prizes. Conclusion: a free annual lottery ticket
worth mentioning to the user when Grand Cup 3 opens, not a $2k-a-month route. The stack is unchanged.

## 1060. User broadens the search (2026-10-25): any automatable income, including services and data products. AP-1 protocol — Apify Store developer economics (S11)

**Rule change (user, 2026-10-25):** the search is no longer only "money in → money out". Fully automatable freelance or custom work, services, data products and marketplaces are in scope,
which relaxes the 10-19 "no products before we profit" rule for this search. The combined automatable stack must still exceed $2k a month, with a legitimate payer and a small start.
**AP-1 (a market measurement, no trial).** Apify Store developers publish scrapers and automations ("Actors") that customers run pay-per-event. Apify bills and pays out 80% of revenue minus compute, and
reported paying $563k a month to developers (Sep 2025), rising to ≈ $1–1.4M a month in 2026. **Data:** public store API (`/v2/store`, top ≈ 15k by popularity; 9,646 unique) plus `/v2/acts/{id}`
`createdAt` for the top 3,000 community actors and a random 1,500 of the rest. **Revenue proxy:** a monthly payout ÷ Σ community paid-actor 30-day users = **$0.93–1.66 per actor-user-month**
(the per-user spend is skewed, so this is a crude average). **Questions (Q1 was already glimpsed on a partial pull of 1,773 rows; Q2 and the bar are fixed before the newcomer analysis is run):** (1) how cohorts by creation half-year reach ≥ 100, 500 and 1,000 30-day users;
(2) **newcomer developers** (earliest sampled actor ≥ 2025-11-01): the distribution of total 30-day users across their actors, and the share reaching ≥ 1,200 (≈ $2k a month at the upper rate);
(3) which niches the newcomers won. **Lead bar:** at least about 10% of newcomer developers with ≥ 10 actors reach ≥ 1,200 users within about 12 months. Otherwise the route is too competitive.

## 1061. AP-1 result: Apify Store newcomers can reach $2k a month in 6–12 months, about 1 in 8 of serious catalog builders. A LEAD (needs the user's free account) (S11)

**No trial (a market measurement; data under the session scratchpad `apify/`, 4,483 actor details).** **Revenue proxy:** $0.93–2.3 per actor-user-month (Apify's payouts were $563k in Sep 2025, then ≈ $1M, with
$1.4M quoted in 2026, divided by 602k community paid-actor 30-day users). **Developers today:** ≈ 75 earn ≥ $2k a month, ≈ 170 earn ≥ $500. **Newcomer developers (Q2)**, by first sampled actor:
| first actor | devs | ≥ 10 actors | of those, ≥ 500 users (≈ $0.5–1.1k) | ≥ 1,200 users (≈ $1.1–2.8k) | ≥ 2,000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-05 → 11 (age 12–18 mo) | 107 | 36 | 19 (53%) | 10 (28%) | 8 |
| 2025-11 → 2026-05 (age 6–12 mo) | 289 | 66 | 20 (30%) | **8 (12%)** | 5 |
| 2026-05 → (age < 6 mo) | 370 | 33 | 2 (6%) | 0 | 0 |
**Bias:** devs whose actors all sit outside the top ≈ 10k by popularity are missing (≈ 87k of 97k store actors are near-zero), so these shares overstate success. The bar (≈ 10% at 12 months) is met
nominally and is perhaps 5–10% after correction. **Ramp:** nobody in the youngest cohort has passed 1,200 users. It takes 6–12 months, then compounds (the 12–18-month cohort: 28%).
**Winners 2025-11 → 2026-05:** zen-studio (45 actors, 12.7k users ≈ $12–29k a month; Chinese platforms Douyin, Xiaohongshu, 1688, Taobao), automation-lab (71, 7.9k; Reddit, FB Ads Library, Trustpilot),
data-slayer (22, 4.2k), blackfalcondata (148, 4.1k). **Where new actors take share** (u30 share new vs old): developer tools 11.8% vs 2.3%, e-commerce 6.1 vs 2.4, AI 5.0 vs 2.4, SEO 2.9 vs 1.3,
MCP servers 1.6 vs 0.2. Old strongholds lose share to them: social 18 vs 27, travel 1 vs 6.
**Effort:** a 98-actor developer reported 15–20 h a week (maintenance 5–7 h, support 3–4 h, about 4–8 h per new actor) for 855 MAU at 6 months. **Automation reading:** runs, billing and payouts are Apify's.
Building, fixing broken scrapers and answering issues is code work that Claude can do on a schedule, and none of it falls to the user beyond the account, KYC and the payout method. **Risks:**
target-site ToS and personal-data scraping, so prefer business, public and e-commerce data and avoid logged-in or personal scraping; it is a 6–12-month ramp; and revenue per user is a crude average.
**Verdict:** the first broadened-search lead that can plausibly clear $2k a month alone, with $0 capital. It needs the user's (free) Apify account to publish, and nothing can be measured further before then.

**Addendum (same day):** apify.com currently shows **"$1.7M paid out last month"**, which puts the proxy at $2.82 per actor-user-month. At that rate ≈ 119 developers earn ≥ $2k a month, and **$2k a month takes ≈ 710 users**,
between the ≥ 500 (30%) and ≥ 1,200 (12%) marks of the 6–12-month newcomer cohort, so roughly 1 in 5 serious newcomers before the selection-bias haircut. The estimate is still crude, since spend per user is skewed.

$0.0001–0.015 per 3 keywords, yet have 9–38 users each. The official actor (0 of 3 results, "SUCCEEDED" with an empty dataset, so its failure rate understates it) keeps 2.7k. **Users do not switch to
better actors; store rank and trust decide.** Ours is a commodity there. (2) **Supply scan, ≈ 120 target sites:** nearly every valuable site has 5–47 actors (Seek has 5, not 3; Walmart 37, Zillow 43).
**Catalog developers (≥ 30 actors) average a median 11 users per actor (p75 38); the median actor has 2.** At $2.82 per user, $2k a month needs ≈ 20 actors at p75 or ≈ 60 at the median. §1061's newcomer
shares were survivors who were **first** on new demand (Chinese platforms, Naver, AI Mode). **This revises AP-1 down:** feasible only as a high-volume catalog aimed at unserved targets, with a 30-day
traction test before scaling. (3) Rejected: AI utilities (no demand on Apify apart from one upscaler), AI-visibility trackers (≤ 65 users each; the official SERP actor already bundles AI engines), Adobe Stock
(DataDome; the clean route is Adobe's keyed API, whose terms bar reselling). (4) **Build 2:** an iStock & Getty Images scraper with keyword-research summaries (total results, freshness of popular results,
contributor concentration, related searches). There were zero actors for iStock, Getty, Dreamstime, 123RF, Depositphotos and Alamy, while Adobe Stock's ≈ 700 contributor-users show an audience. CloudFront's WAF rejected
httpx from Apify IPs, including residential; **curl_cffi Chrome impersonation passes even on datacenter proxies.** Test: 6 query×site combinations, 1,080 assets plus summaries, about 90 s.

## 1066. AP-1 build 3: Dreamstime scraper (download counts, level, keywords), the only stock agency publishing per-image sales (S11)

**No trial.** StockX was checked and dropped: 8 actors, ≤ 22 users, so demand on Apify is thin. **Dreamstime** had zero actors, and its image pages show **downloads** and a 0–5 **level** (sales-based price tier). Structured data
carries the full keyword list, creator and publish date. The actor collects search results (80 per page), opens each image page through a worker pool (one proxy session per worker, rotated only on block, paced),
pushes rows incrementally, and writes a keyword summary: download median/P90, level mix, upload-year mix, top keywords weighted by downloads, top contributors and best sellers. **Blocking:** Cloudflare burned the free
plan's 5 datacenter IPs at 6 parallel requests, so **residential is the default** at a measured **$0.0006 per result** in proxy traffic (5.8 MB per 81 pages, compressed). Under PPE the developer pays that, so it must sit inside the price.
Test: 2 queries × 160, 320 rows, 0 errors, $0.19 total. About 20% of results are 2026 uploads whose stats Dreamstime hides (`statsShown: false`). Credit used so far $1.58 of $5.

## 1067. AP-1 builds 4–6 (SEEK 8-market jobs, Envato Market, Nordic marketplaces); competitor benchmark; a substring error in one demand figure (S11)

**No trial.** All are private and unpublished, with code in `~/apify-actors`. (1) **Seek/Jobstreet/JobsDB**: one JSON search API plus GraphQL `jobDetails` serves 8 markets (AU, NZ, MY, SG, PH, ID, HK, TH), with ≈ 950 users across
the rival per-country actors. Head-to-head (AU "accountant", 50 jobs): ours 12 s and $0.0009; blackfalcondata 31 s, 78 fields, with applicant insights, alerts and incremental mode; websift 14 s, with applicant numbers and
contacts; bovi 15 s, no descriptions. **Gap closed:** added GraphQL `insights` (applicant count/volume, resume and cover-letter %), screening questions, isLinkOut/apply URL, review count, contacts in the ad text, and
an only-new-jobs mode (a named KV store; verified 0 overlap across two runs). Our remaining edges are the 8 markets in one run, salaries parsed into numbers, and price. (2) **Envato Market** (ThemeForest,
CodeCanyon, AudioJungle, 3DOcean): sales, price, rating and reviews are on the search cards. Each site's firewall accepts different fingerprints (ThemeForest wants Safari plus residential; the others Chrome plus
datacenter), so the actor rotates fingerprint × proxy type and remembers what worked: 480 items, 100 s, $0.013. GraphicRiver is blocked, and VideoHive/PhotoDune show no sales, so they are excluded. (3) **Nordic** (Tori, FINN, Blocket, DBA:
one Vend "recommerce" platform; base64 react-query state embedded in the page; Product LD for details): 480 listings, 39 s, $0.002. **Correction:** "Tori 546 users" came from a substring match on
"s-tori-es" (Instagram Stories actors). Real Tori demand is ≈ 4 users, and FINN/Blocket/DBA ≈ 125, so this is a low-demand bet. Rejected along the way: Depositphotos (obfuscated JS state), Alamy (client-side API),
Vecteezy (no public stats), StockX/Steam (≤ 22 users per actor), Adobe Stock (DataDome), most EU classifieds (15–45 actors each). Credit used ≈ $1.7 of $5.

## §1085 — F-family 3 protocol: are options-implied probabilities a better forecast of "close above K" questions than a realized-vol model? (S11)

**No trial at registration; written BEFORE any outcome is joined.** Metaculus's API now requires an account even to read (403), so the
§1044 module is tested on synthetic Market-Pulse-style questions. **Questions:** for 21 underlyings (SPY, NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL,
META, TSLA, AVGO, AMD, NFLX, JPM, XOM, LLY, COST, WMT, ORCL, PLTR, MU, INTC, BA), every 5th DoltHub snapshot date (post-no-preference/options)
from 2020-01, each listed expiration 5–60 calendar days out, each call strike with delta in [0.03, 0.97]: "will the close on the expiration
date be above K?" Outcome: Yahoo daily close on the expiration date (previous close if closed). **Forecasts:** (M) module p = N(N⁻¹(Δ) − σ√T)
with σ the strike's implied vol, T = days/365 (risk-neutral P(S_T > K)); (M_c) the same with σ × c, c fitted on 2020–2023 by Brier on a
0.70–1.10 grid (variance-premium correction); (B) baseline lognormal, zero drift, σ = 20-session realized vol of daily log returns, S = the
snapshot date's close. **Periods:** train 2020-01 → 2023-12 (fit c only); sealed = snapshot dates 2024-01 → expirations ≤ 2026-10-23.
**Read (sealed):** Brier and log-score difference M − B (and M_c − B), paired, clustered by (underlying, date); calibration by forecast bin,
with the tails (p < 0.15, p > 0.85) reported separately. **Pass:** M or M_c beats B on Brier with clustered t ≥ 2 AND the tail bins are
calibrated within ±3 points or 2 SE. Pass → the module is worth wiring into a Metaculus bot once the user has an account; fail → §1044's
edge is not demonstrated and the Metaculus route rests on F2 alone.

## §1086 — F3 result: options-implied probabilities beat the realized-vol model (t −3.6) but fail the tail-calibration clause on the upper tail — FAIL by protocol (S11)

**No trial.** 222,961 questions (train 73,828; sealed 149,133, 2,537 underlying × date clusters). `reports/f3_threshold.json`.
**Accuracy (sealed):** module Brier 0.14464 vs baseline 0.14598, diff −0.00134 (clustered t −3.55); log score −0.0081 (t −3.99).
c fitted on train = 1.025 (no variance-premium shrink); M_c t −2.83. **Calibration (sealed, module):** p < 0.05: 3.6% predicted vs 3.5%
observed; 0.05–0.15: 9.4% vs 11.2%; 0.95+: 95.6% vs 98.3%; **0.85–0.95: 90.6% vs 96.3% — outside ±3 points and 2 SE → FAIL.** The
baseline is far worse in the tails (p < 0.05: 1.6% predicted vs 6.0% observed). **Reading:** the miss is upward drift — risk-neutral
odds carry no equity premium and 2024–26 was a strong rally (sealed: all questions 48.6% predicted vs 53.8% observed; even INTC +6.6
points; train 2020–23 gap +3.0 points and its 0.85–0.95 bin calibrated, 90.7% vs 89.5%). Downside long shots — where LLM bots are worst
— are calibrated. A drift correction is a new hypothesis: it can only be tested forward. Decision: no Metaculus account on F3's
strength; the route rests on F2 (11-09). Module kept (`forecast/market_implied.py`).

## §1088 — A120 protocol: a strategy fitted to each prop firm's own rules, at zero edge (user request 2026-10-28) (S10)

**No trial; written before the grid is run.** User: the Tradeify plan is known to fail other firms (§766: consistency and qualifying-
day gates destroy the one-big-bracket option); find a different, rule-fitted strategy per firm with positive EV. **Rules (2026, from
third-party summaries, checked 2026-10-28; to verify at checkout):** Topstep 50K Combine $49/month + $149 activation, target $3,000,
EOD MLL $2,000, best day ≤ 50% of target; XFA Standard: 5 winning days ≥ $150, payout ≤ 50% of balance up to $2,000, min $125, MLL
fixed at the start after the first payout, 90%; XFA Consistency: 3 days, best day ≤ 40% of cycle profit, ≤ 50% up to $3,000. Apex 50K
EOD: eval $349 list (often 80% off) + $119 activation, target $3,000, $2,000 EOD, $1,000 DLL; PA: safety net $52,100, 5 days ≥ $250,
best day < 50% of profit since the last payout, caps $1.5k/1.5k/2k/2.5k/2.5k/3k, min $500, 100%, 6 payouts then closed. LucidFlex 50K:
$138 one-time, target $3,000, $2,000 EOD, 40% eval consistency; funded: 5 days ≥ $150, ≤ 50% of profit up to $2,000, min $500, no
consistency, no buffer, 90%, 5 payouts then treated as ended (live unmodelled). Tradeify Select Daily kept as a fixed-bracket reference.
**Strategy family:** one MNQ bracket a day (take W, stop L in $, contracts = round(max(W,L)/$600)), separate (W, L) for evaluation and
funded, sides randomised daily (4 seeds) on A23 MNQ RTH paths; W ∈ {150…1,500}, L ∈ {150…2,000}. **Selection:** chosen on one era
(2010-20 or 2021-26) and scored on the other. **Read:** a firm is a candidate only if its policy chosen on EITHER era is positive on the
OTHER era by ≥ $500 a run; dollars are approximate (rule fidelity is the main risk, as §766 showed), the sign is the finding.

**Topstep XFA Standard** +$1,294 / +$743; LucidFlex +$616 / +$159 (only one direction ≥ $500 — marginal); Apex at list −$442 / −$447,
at 80% off −$119 / +$16; Tradeify fixed-bracket reference +$884 (its solved policy is better, §806). **The Topstep strategy:** evaluation
take $1,250 / stop up to the full $2,000 (best day stays under the 50% consistency mark, ~3 days to pass, a cheap monthly Combine to
retry); funded take $650 / stop $2,000 (≈ 75% winning days), payout as soon as eligible (≤ 50% of balance), then the MLL sits at the
start and the next loss usually ends the account — buy the next Combine. Value comes from cheap re-entry plus early payouts.

pricing +$258 / +$564 (43%). Standard path: +$1,100 / +$1,172 → +$144 / +$39 in the worst variant. **Candidate (structural, zero edge):**
≈ $330-430 a month per slot at the base terms, ≈ $65-140 in the worst; Topstep allows 5 XFAs (≈ $1.6-2.1k / $0.3-0.7k a month total).
Open: Combine price ($49 vs $85/month) and DLL, the bot rules (API allowed via ProjectX, not on live accounts; third parties report
"personal device only"), Live Funded Account terms (unmodelled), and accounts must trade the SAME side or different markets (opposite
positions across accounts = prohibited hedging).

## §1093 — Screen: Darwinex Zero / DarwinIA SILVER (performance fees on allocated capital, bots allowed, US not restricted) — closed: capped by subscription vs a 15% fee on risk-normalised returns (S11)

**No trial (desk, 2026-10-29).** Shape fits §1053 (someone else's capital, code allowed): Darwinex Zero is a simulated account (€45/month+, EAs allowed, the
US is not on the restricted list per third parties); DARWINs rated ≥ 75 each month (22% current-month return, 67% six-month return, 11% max drawdown) get
a SILVER allocation of €30k (minimum) up to €375k (top rank), held 3 months, up to 3 overlapping; the trader earns 15% of the allocation's profit above a
high-water mark, quarterly; one free €25k booster if nothing is allocated in the first 6 months; DARWINs from the same user must correlate < 0.5. **Ceiling
at zero edge:** DARWIN returns are risk-normalised (leverage cannot buy variance), so a 3-month allocation's expected positive return ≈ 0.4 × σ(3 mo) ≈ 3%;
fee ≈ 15% × 3% × €30-80k ≈ €130-360 per allocation. Even at an optimistic 30% monthly allocation rate that is ≈ €40-110/month per subscription against
€45, and extra subscriptions need uncorrelated DARWINs. Below the bar before any data; a real edge would be traded directly instead. Closed.
Sources: darwinexzero.document360.io (DarwinIA SILVER, performance fees), luxalgo.com (restricted countries), mql5.com blog 776722 (rating weights, €45).

up, dipped through the raised floor and recovered counted as surviving. `reporting/a122_fast_track_minute.py` walks every 1-minute bar of the trade in the worst
order (raise the peak by the bar's high, test the low against the floor, then the stop, then the take). One slot, continuous timeline, re-buy next session,

## §1105 — Bulenox due diligence for the Fast Track plan: pays in most cases; denial risks are discretionary (flip days), and any bot needs written approval (S10)

**Desk, 2026-10-29.** Reputation: Trustpilot 4.5-4.8 across mirrors, many reports of repeated payouts; PropFirmCircle lists it "Not Recommended" (34+ trader reports of
vague, unevenly applied rules) but "not a scam". Recurring denial reason: the **flipping / flip-day rule** in the Master Agreement (not in the help center): third parties
describe ≤ 2 "insignificant activity" days per rolling 10 trading days, no published thresholds; consequences warnings → payout review/denial → closure. The plan trades
the same full size every day, so its days are not minimal-activity days, but its time-exit days (≈ 3-6% on MNQ, ≈ 20% on MGC London) can end near flat. **Terms of Use
(bulenox.com/legal/Terms_of_Use.pdf), "Algorithms and Auto Trading":** no scalping algorithms or rapid-trade bots; "any third-party algorithm, automated trading software …
must be reviewed and approved by the Bulenox management team before use"; the $100/month third-party API / trade-copier fee "does not constitute approval". Nothing
published forbids a stop equal to the drawdown or one trade a day. **Implication:** run the plan with manual brackets (≤ 10% effort: one order per account per day; a
copier costs $100/month and still needs approval), and before scaling past one account ask Bulenox support in writing whether (a) a daily bracket whose stop equals the
drawdown and (b) identical brackets across up to five Fast Track accounts are acceptable, and how a flip day is defined. Payout-denial risk is not in any of the
§1095-§1103 numbers.

## §1113 — S-family 1 protocol: aggregate short interest as a half-monthly sign for MNQ (Rapach, Ringgenberg & Zhou 2016), current regime (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; N 1,562 → one trial on the sealed read.** Overnight search (user 2026-10-29: ≥ $2k/month, ≤ 10% effort). Why this
fits: it trades MNQ (small margin, prop-account eligible), once per half-month, fully automatable; no aggregate equity short-interest series has been tested here (CFTC
positioning was, §604). **Data:** FINRA `consolidatedShortInterest` (free API, no key; history starts 2018-12), every settlement date, restricted to the `pack.npz` liquid
names. **Signal:** S = log(equal-weighted mean days-to-cover) across names with ADV > 0, minus its mean over the previous 24 reports (causal detrend). **Timing:** FINRA
publishes ≈ 7 business days after settlement, so S is usable at the close of the 10th `pack.npz` session after the settlement date; held to the next report's usable close.
**Rule:** S > 0 (short interest high) → short MNQ, else long (the paper's sign). **Target:** QQQ adjusted close-to-close over each holding period. **Statistic (strict rule
§119):** x = (rule − always long) × r; CONFIRM needs t > 1.645, circular-shift placebo ≥ 95th (2,000 shifts of the signal series), and mean x > 0. **Split:** discovery
2020-12 → 2022-12 (first 24 reports are warm-up); sealed 2023-01 → latest, read once. A discovery mean ≤ 0 closes it without a sealed read.

## §1114 — S-family 2 protocol: the CBOE equity put/call ratio as a contrarian next-session sign for MNQ, current regime (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; one trial on the sealed read.** Untested here (no put/call series in any family). **Data:** CBOE equity put/call
ratio, daily: `equitypc.csv` (2006-11 → 2019-10-04) plus the daily `market_statistics/daily/{date}_daily_options` JSON ("EQUITY PUT/CALL RATIO", 2019-10-07 →). Published
after the close. **Signal:** P = 5-session mean of the ratio ÷ its 60-session mean − 1, known at the close of day d. **Rule:** P > 0 (puts heavy: fear) → long the next
session close-to-close, else short. **Target:** QQQ adjusted close d → d+1 (MNQ proxy). **Statistic (strict rule §119):** x = (rule − always long) × r; CONFIRM needs t > 1.645,
circular-shift placebo ≥ 95th (2,000 shifts), mean x > 0. Costs: 0.25 MNQ point a side on each flip (≈ 0.003% at NQ 20k), charged to x. **Split:** discovery 2007-03 → 2022-12;
sealed 2023-01 → latest, read once. A discovery mean ≤ 0 closes it.

## §1115 — S-family 3 protocol: market breadth (share of liquid stocks above their 50-session mean) as a contrarian next-session sign for MNQ, current regime (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; one trial on the sealed read.** Family 159 (§558) tested the RSP − SPY *return* spread; the breadth *level* was
not. **Data:** `pack.npz` adjusted closes (2,012 liquid US names, 2015-01 → 2026-10). **Signal at the close of d:** B = share of names (with 50 prior closes) above their
50-session mean; z = B − mean of B over the previous 250 sessions. **Rule:** z < 0 (washed out) → long QQQ close d → d+1, else short. **Statistic, costs, placebo:** as §1114.
**Split:** discovery 2016-01 → 2022-12; sealed 2023-01 → latest, read once. A discovery mean ≤ 0 closes it.

## §1116 — S-family 3 discovery: breadth is not a contrarian sign for MNQ — −6.44 bp a session, t −1.67; closed without a sealed read. NAAIM: data behind scripts (S1)

**No trial (discovery fail, §1115).** `stocks/s3_breadth.py`, 1,714 sessions 2016-01 → 2022-12, long on 48% of them. The sign runs the other way (weak breadth → weaker
next day), but reversing it after seeing it would be a new, data-led hypothesis; not registered. NAAIM exposure index: the site serves the series only through

## §1117 — S-family 4 protocol: the off-exchange short-volume ratio (a "DIX"-style dealer-buying gauge) as a next-session sign for MNQ, current regime (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; one trial on the sealed read.** Mechanism claimed by SqueezeMetrics (2017, "Short Is Long"): off-exchange short
volume is mostly market makers selling into customer buying, so a high ratio marks buying pressure. **Data:** FINRA Reg SHO consolidated daily files
(`cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/CNMSshvol{YYYYMMDD}.txt`, published the same evening), 2018-08 →. **Signal at the close of d:** D = Σ ShortVolume × price ÷
Σ TotalVolume × price over the 500 `pack.npz` names with the largest prior-60-session dollar volume (price = that day's `pack` close); z = D − mean of D over the previous
60 sessions. **Rule:** z > 0 → long QQQ close d → d+1, else short. **Statistic, costs, placebo:** as §1114. **Split:** discovery 2018-11 → 2022-12; sealed 2023-01 → latest,
read once. A discovery mean ≤ 0 closes it.

## §1118 — S-family 5 protocol: aggregate insider buying (Seyhun 1988; Lakonishok & Lee 2001) as a weekly sign for MNQ, 2007-2026 (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; one trial on the sealed read.** I-family 1 (§913-915) tested stock-level drift after purchases; the *aggregate*
insider buy/sell balance as a market-timing sign has not been tested. **Data:** SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets (Form 4 and 4/A, quarterly, 2006Q1 →), officers and
directors only, open-market non-derivative trades: code P (buy) and S (sale). **Signal at each Friday close:** b = purchase filings ÷ (purchase + sale filings), by filing
date, over the last 20 sessions; z = b − mean of the weekly b over the previous 52 weeks. **Rule:** z > 0 (insiders buying more than usual) → long QQQ Friday close → next
Friday close, else short. **Statistic, placebo:** as §1114, on weeks; cost charged on flips. **Split:** discovery 2007-06 → 2022-12; sealed 2023-01 → latest, read once.
A discovery mean ≤ 0 closes it.

## §1125 — D-series family 176 protocol: the four S-series gauges as every-day signs for the non-equity markets, current regime (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; N 1,562.** Gauges known at the close of day d (constructions exactly as §1114/§1115/§1117/§1118): put/call P,
breadth z, short-volume z, insider z (latest weekly value). Each gauge's sign gives side = +1 when it reads "risk-on" (P < 0, breadth z > 0, short-volume z > 0, insider z > 0)
else −1. **Targets:** next weekday's open → close (d10 series, bps) for GC, SI, HG, CL, NG, ZN, 6E, 6J, ZC, ZS, ZW, RTY; rules **follow** (side) and **fade** (−side):
4 × 12 × 2 = 96 cells. Cost d12.COST per session. **Discovery** 2018-11 → 2022-12 (d24.DISC, from the short-volume start): carry if mean > 0 and t > 1.96; at most 5
carried, by t. **Sealed** 2023-01 → 2026-08 (d24.VAL), each carried cell read once (one trial each): CONFIRM needs net t > 1.645, against-always-long t > 1.645
(§119), circular-shift placebo ≥ 95th.

## §1127 — D-series family 177 protocol: the weekly natural-gas storage surprise against its 5-year norm as a week-long sign for NG (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; N 1,563.** Untested here (families 40/89 used EIA crude only). **Data:** EIA weekly Lower-48 working gas
(`NW2_EPG0_SWO_R48_BCFw.xls`, week ending Friday, released the next Thursday 10:30 ET), 2010 →. **Surprise:** u = this week's change − mean change of the same ISO week
in the previous 5 years. **Trade:** the 5 weekdays after the release Thursday (Fri → Thu), summed open → close returns of NG (d10 series, bps; open → close only, so
the continuous contract's roll gaps are excluded), cost d12.COST × 5. **Cells:** follow fundamentals (u > 0 → short, else long) and fade (opposite): 2 cells. **Discovery**
2015-01 → 2022-12: carry if mean > 0, t > 1.96. **Sealed** 2023-01 → 2026-08 once per carried cell, strict rule as §1125.

## §1129 — D-series family 178 protocol: Treasury coupon-auction strength as a next-session sign for ZN (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; N 1,563.** Auction outcomes have not been a predictor here (K4 used only the auction calendar). **Data:** Fiscal
Data `auctions_query` (free, no key): Notes and Bonds, 2009 →. Each auction's term bucket = years in `security_term` rounded (a 9-Year 10-Month reopening is the 10-year).
**Strength measures:** (a) bid-to-cover − mean of the previous 6 auctions in the same bucket; (b) indirect share (indirect accepted ÷ total accepted) − the same mean.
A day with several auctions takes the mean across them. **Trade:** ZN next weekday open → close (d10 bps), cost d12.COST; strong (> 0) → long for **follow**, short for
**fade**: 2 measures × 2 rules = 4 cells. **Discovery** 2010-01 → 2022-12: carry if mean > 0, t > 1.96. **Sealed** 2023-01 → 2026-08, strict rule as §1125.

## §1133 — D-series family 179 protocol: weekly momentum/reversal in commodity futures, cross-sectional and own-market (KAIST short-term commodity momentum) (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; N 1,563.** Universe: GC, SI, HG, CL, NG, ZC, ZS, ZW (d10 daily open → close, bps; overnight and roll gaps
excluded). Each market's weekly return = sum of its open → close moves Mon-Fri, in risk units (÷ its daily sd over the previous 60 sessions × √5). **Cells:**
(1) cross-sectional: next week long the top 2 and short the bottom 2 by last week's risk-unit return — **follow**; (2) the same **fade**; (3) own-market: each market takes
the sign of its own last week, pooled equal-risk — **follow**; (4) the same **fade**. 4 cells; weekly return in risk units net of d12.COST × 5 per leg. **Discovery**
2010-03 → 2022-12: carry if mean > 0 and t > 1.96. **Sealed** 2023-01 → 2026-08, once per carried cell: CONFIRM needs t > 1.645 and circular-shift placebo ≥ 95th
(the cells are market-neutral or two-sided, so the always-long leg of §119 is the pooled-long benchmark: the cell must also beat it with t > 1.645).

## §1135 — D-series family 180 protocol: ACM 10-year term-premium shocks as signs for ZN and ES two sessions later (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; N 1,563.** Untested here. **Data:** NY Fed `ACMTermPremium.xls` daily ACMTP10 (1961 →). The publication lag is
unclear, so a value dated d is used only for the session after next (d+2). **Event:** |ΔTP10| > 2 × sd of the previous 60 daily changes. **Cells:** ZN and ES, d+2 open →
close (d10 bps, d12.COST); **follow** = side −sign(ΔTP) (a rising premium continues to weigh on bonds and stocks), **fade** = the opposite: 4 cells. **Discovery**
2010-03 → 2022-12, carry if mean > 0 and t > 1.96; **sealed** 2023-01 → 2026-08, strict rule as §1125.

policy (the Oct-2025 trade-up change); closed. Nothing new clears the bar.

## §1140 — D-series family 181 protocol: VIX-settlement Wednesdays (SOQ at the open; Griffin & Shams 2018) in ES and NQ (S1)

**Written and committed BEFORE any statistic is computed; N 1,563.** Untested here. **Dates:** each month's VIX expiry = the third Friday of the following month − 30 days
(a Wednesday), moved to the prior weekday if that is not a d10 trading day, 2010-03 →. **Cells:** ES, NQ × {expiry-day open → close, next-day open → close} × {long, short}
= 8 cells (d10 bps, d12.COST). Drift-neutral reading: each cell's mean is compared with the same market's mean on all other days (excess = cell − that mean, sign-
matched). **Discovery** 2010-03 → 2022-12: carry if excess > 0 and t > 1.96 (t of the cell's event returns minus the other-day mean). **Sealed** 2023-01 → 2026-08 once per
carried cell: CONFIRM needs net t > 1.645, against-always-long t > 1.645, placebo (random Wednesdays, 2,000 draws) ≥ 95th.

trading day of the month before (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov). **Cells:** GC × {the 3 sessions before FND summed, FND day, the day after} × {long, short} = 6 cells, open →
close (roll gaps excluded), read as §1140 (drift-neutral excess against non-overlapping blocks of the same length; discovery 2010-03 → 2022-12, carry if excess > 0 and
t > 1.96; sealed strict rule; placebo random trading days).

## §1155 — Family 186: gold first notice day — 2 of 6 carried; sealed: pre-FND short REJECT (t01564), day-after long WATCHLIST (t01565); N 1,563 → 1,565 (S1)

`reporting/d186_goldfnd.py`; `reports/d186_discovery.json`, `d186_sealed.json`. Discovery 2010-03 → 2022-12 (77 FNDs): short the 3 sessions before FND +30.8 bp vs other
3-session blocks (t +2.47); long the day after +28.8 bp (t +2.26) — the liquidation-and-recovery story. **Sealed 2023-01 → 2026-08 (22 FNDs): pre-FND short −44.7 bp a
trade (t −1.08, placebo 39th) → REJECT; day-after long +14.3 bp (t +0.50, placebo 55th) → WATCHLIST** (positive, far from the strict rule; the against-always-long
test is undefined for a long-only cell). Six events a year at ≈ $14 per MGC contract would not matter to the stack even if it held. Watchlist only.

$210; SN22 Desearch $203; SN50 Synth $203 / $202. Many subnets pay one owner UID or almost nothing to the median miner.

a time-of-day vol profile × fast EWMA level (half-life 0.5-1 h, reverting to the 7-day level over 2-3 h) with residuals standardised by local vol, scaled 0.9-0.95, works best.

competition vs the median UID's 0.33%.** ≈ $75/month per UID from Crypto-24h alone at today's prices; other assets and the other three competitions not yet built.

## §1165 — SN83 CliqueAI (maximum clique) benchmarked on 513 logged problems: the field is strong; our solvers tie the best on ≈ 70-85% — not yet competitive (S11)

`synth/clique_data.py`). Graphs are dense (density 0.70-0.95, 290-900 vertices, time limits 6-30 s), all distinct (no repeated degree sequences). On a typical problem
90-100% of miners reach the best size; on ≈ 1 in 4 only 4-20% do, and those decide ratings (a smaller clique scores ≈ 1/3 of the best via exp(−pr/rel)).
Our C solvers on 60 problems (30% of the time limit, one core): DLS-MC 32 ties / 28 short; greedy+DLS-MC 33 / 27; **NuMVC on the complement 43 / 17**; 8 parallel NuMVC
seeds fix some misses but one 900-vertex problem every miner solves at 79 stays at 77; a beam-greedy copy of a public fork's method is worse (73-74). A public fork shows
operators hash graphs (bliss canonical form) to share work across their many UIDs. Median UID ≈ $509/month, burn ≈ $38: attractive only with a top-tier solver; parked
behind SN50. Code: `synth/dlsmc.c`, `dlsmc2.c`, `numvc.c`, `beam.c`, `clique_bench.py`.

## §1171 — SN101 Tag101 (tagging X posts): a flat payout where a reference miner should sit near the median — ≈ $280-370 per UID a month for a $6 registration (S11)

**No trial (desk + chain).** Task: return K short tags for a post (validators pull posts from a public whitelist of AI-related X accounts); each tag is scored on
cluster support among miners (log-scaled distinct-miner count), proximity to its cluster's centre, stability, validity and label fitness — a consensus score.
Identical tag sets are scaled down only when ~50 miners share one (c = 50, p = 5.5). Reference miner (`tasks/sn101_reference/core/miner.py`): one OpenAI-compatible
chat call (gpt-4o-mini by default; `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and `OPENAI_MODEL` are configurable), 3 tags as a JSON array — ≈ $0.0001 a call. **Chain (TAO $239): 247 miners,
only 16 under $100 a month; percentiles 10/25/50/75/90 = $155 / $281 / $291 / $369 / $373; total ≈ $71.5k a month; registration burn 0.025 TAO (≈ $6).** SN101 pool
3,452 TAO (≈ $0.82M) — selling a few $k a month moves it ≈ 0.3%. Reading: a miner with a decent LLM should earn near the median; 10 UIDs ≈ $2.8-3.7k a month before
alpha-price changes and the ≈ 4% dilution they cause. Needs: an LLM API key (user's choice of provider; open-weight providers work through the OpenAI-compatible
URL), a VPS with a public port, the user's wallet. Risks: SN101 alpha price ($0.81) and the subnet's emission share can fall; the scorer can change; posts come from
X (the miner only reads the post text the validator sends).

## §1175 — SN101 day 1: both UIDs below the median; cause = the repeated-set penalty on reference tags; m1 switched to an "uncommon set" tagger (A/B vs m2) (S11)

**No trial (live).** By 11:00 UTC 10-30 both UIDs had answered every task (≈ 166 each since midnight) but earned little: m2 peaked at $294/month (04:00) and slid to
$106; m1 ≈ $0.4. All 8 validators agree (per-validator weight: median miner ≈ 0.44%, UID 181 ≈ 0.11-0.14%, UID 104 ≈ 0.001%). Cause found in the scorer
(`tasks/sn101_reference/core/scoring/tag_scorer.py`): each miner's score is multiplied by 1 / (1 + (k/50)^5.5), k = miners whose tokenised tag SET is identical;
the stock reference prompt (gpt-4o-mini, 3 tags) gives the same obvious sets as everyone else running it. Fix (`/opt/tag101/repo/tasks/ourtags.py`, loaded with
`--task.miner_module tag101.tasks.ourtags`, TAG_SEED per miner): the model ranks 6 candidate tags; submit the top one plus 2 seeded-random picks from ranks 2-5 —
every tag on-consensus, the set rarely identical to anyone's. Deployed on m1 at ≈ 11:40 UTC; m2 stays on the reference for comparison. m1's 24 h immunity ends
≈ 01:00 UTC 10-31.

## §1180 — SN5 Hone deep look: flat ≈ $1,050 per UID because pay ∝ pass rate and farms submit one answer from many UIDs; the cost of solving every task decides it (S11)

**No trial (desk).** Repo hone-subnet-org/hone-subnet (53454a9). Tasks: real repositories with planted defects or terminal incident tasks, graded in a pinned Docker
sandbox by hidden checks; the answer is a unified diff or a Bash script plus a trajectory; the demo miner is an agent with read-only workspace tools (≤ 48 calls)
on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint — default **Kimi K3 (open-weight) on Amazon Bedrock**, so an open model fits the terms constraint. **Pay:** a full pass earns
1 (≥ 0.95 with a light speed tiebreak), a fail 0; each UID's weight = mean payment over its last ≤ 100 tasks, L1-normalised — linear in pass rate. **Volume:**
one task per validator every 38 blocks (≈ 7.6 min) to 128 of 256 miners; 11 validators → up to ≈ 2,000 tasks a day; byte-identical submissions are graded once,
so an operator solves each task once and submits it from all its UIDs — hence the flat p10 $944 / median $1,053 / p90 $1,098. **Economics:** income ≈ $1,050 ×
UIDs at the field's pass rate; cost ≈ tasks/day × agent cost per task (unknown: plausibly $0.05-0.30 with an open model) — ≈ $3-18k a month for an operator that
answers everything, nearly independent of how many UIDs it runs. Viable only with several UIDs and a cheap model at the field's pass rate. Burn 0.432 TAO (≈ $100).
Unknowns to measure before any spend: our agent's pass rate on the two retired fixtures (Docker, pinned image) and its tokens per task.

## §1182 — SN79 MVTRX (simulated-exchange trading) screened: a real strategy competition, fourth in line (S11)

**No trial (desk).** Repo taos-im/sn-79 (0.6.6). Miners run trading agents over 128 simulated limit-order books (C++ MAXE engine) against background agents;
≈ 95% of rewards from trading, split equally into **making** (spread captured on maker fills on both sides of a book, judged by the price shortly afterwards;
smoothed over ≈ 3 simulated hours) and **skill** (mark-to-market P&L minus average inventory × the book's move — de-beta'd alpha — on a minimum number of books);
≈ 5% for optional GenTRX gradient training (GPU helps). Latency is penalised; a capital-turnover cap limits volume; new simulation configs ≈ weekly; public
dashboards (taos.simulate.trading) show per-miner activity. Miners need ≈ 1 GB RAM each; strategy work needs the simulator (validators run 32 GB / 16 cores).
Chain: median miner UID ≈ $253/month, p10 $53, burn ≈ $22, 45 operators (top-5 46%). Fit: our market-making / short-term research; cost: a bigger server and
real strategy development. Order of additions: Tag101 (fixing) → ReadyAI → Synth → MVTRX → Hone.

## §1184 — SN33 ReadyAI scoring study: cosine to the validator's own full-conversation tags, cubed weights, a 25% owner burn since 10-27 (S11)

**No trial (desk).** Repo afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project (37b4474). The validator tags the FULL conversation itself (GPT-4o default) and
averages those tags' embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large) into one "neighbourhood" vector; a miner sees only a window. Each miner tag scores its cosine to
that vector (≤ 20 tags scored, ≥ 3 required); score = 0.55 × mean of the top 3 UNIQUE tags (not exactly in the validator's set) + 0.25 × mean + 0.10 × median +
0.10 × max; penalties: no exact matches × 0.9, < 1-3 unique tags × 0.85-0.95, max < 0.2 × 0.5, < 2 tags × 0.2. Validator EMA (half alpha on zero rewards) →
normalised → **cubed** (nonlinear_power 3): a 10% better score earns ≈ 33% more weight, so the flat payout reflects a field of near-identical default miners.
**Owner burn: 25% of emissions since 2026-10-27** (today's chain medians already reflect it, ≈ $194). Other task types exist (webpage metadata, skill coverage).
Plan for a ReadyAI slot: (1) a few tags the validator would also produce (avoid the no-match penalty) plus several distinct tags close to the conversation's
centre (the top-3 unique term is 55%); (2) pick tags by our own text-embedding-3-large cosine to the centroid of a broad candidate set; (3) an offline lab on
ReadyAI's public Hugging Face conversations with GPT-4o full-conversation tags as the stand-in ground truth. Needs the bigger server for live slots (8 GB).

## §1190 — SN101: why both UIDs earn little — softmax pay, inherited UID history, and our answers ≈ 0.28 below the field (S11)

**No trial (live diagnosis).** From Tag101 1.1.1 source: validators score with `rolling_ma_softmax` (not the EMA assumed in §1175/§1177): per-UID mean raw
reward over the last 24 h (missing rounds count as 0), then softmax with β = 10; weights = stake-weighted mean of the validators' softmaxed scoreboards
(owner validator UID 0 holds ≈ 84% of validator alpha stake). Rounds every 15 min. So ln(w_i / w_j) / 10 = mean-raw-score gap. On-chain incentive inverted
(18:10 UTC): 75% of the 248 miners sit within 0.04 of the best (the 117-UID operator −0.021..−0.036; ≈ 40 small operators similar); UID 181 (m2) −0.23,
UID 104 (m1) −0.57. The scoreboard's raw history is keyed by UID and never reset when the hotkey changes, so each new registrant inherits the pruned
occupant's last-24 h rewards: this, not the port, explains §1181 (m1's UID inherited ≈ 0, m2's ≈ median; port test moot). m2's slide fits
avg(t) = prior·(1 − t/24) + ours·t/24 with ours ≈ prior − 0.28 (predicted −0.12 / −0.198 vs the median at 11:00 / 18:03 UTC; observed −0.10 / −0.197),
the same line through the stock (to 15:20) and entity3 periods — entity3 changed nothing visible. The lab crowd (§1177-§1179) is therefore not the live
crowd. Validator reach confirmed (25-min SYN capture): owner 54.177.95.135, 34.70.162.213 (UID 61) and two more IPs (≈ UIDs 56/60) hit both miners every
≈ 15 min; the 4 near-zero-stake validators send nothing (irrelevant to weights). Inherited history rolls off ≈ 01:00 UTC 10-31 (registration block
9393200/9393207); afterwards the hourly weight change measures our current answers directly (Δgap/h ≈ 4·(new − dropped)/96 for the owner validator).
Projection with today's answers: m2 ≈ $15-20/month. Next: a live arm with a different answer style on m1 (pending the user's approval), read by slope.

## §1192 — ReadyAI scaling prep: the stock miner busy-loops (≈ 40% CPU each); fix + usage logging built; field ceiling ≈ $280/slot (S11)

**No trial (desk + live read, 21:30 UTC 10-30).** (1) CPU: each ReadyAI miner holds ≈ 35-50% of the droplet's single core while idle (top, 3 × 5 s).
Cause: `BaseMinerNeuron.run` waits for `block - metagraph.last_update[uid] >= epoch_length`, always true for a miner (miners never set weights), so it
calls `sync()` (registration check + full metagraph resync + save_state) back to back. Fix in `deploy/sn33/run_miner.py`: `sync()` throttled to once per
SYNC_SECONDS (300); only the run-loop thread calls it (validators reach the axon independently). (2) Cost: ReadyAI sends five task types, not only
tagging — since 17:00 UTC r1/r2 received conversation_tagging 14/9, skill_generation 7/9, skill_coverage_evaluation 10/3, named_entities 1/0,
webpage_metadata 0/1; skill generation chains several long-output calls. No upstream token logging, so the launcher now wraps the OpenAI client's
chat/embedding `create` and appends the reported tokens per call to USAGE_LOG (dry-run on the droplet: patched, one embed row logged). (3) Memory:
r1/r2 ≈ 280-370 MB RSS each, m1 ≈ 390 MB (spaCy), m2 ≈ 100 MB; ≈ 660 MB available of 1.97 GB. (4) Chain (TAO $234.5): wallet free 0.1268 TAO;
ReadyAI burn 0.0413 TAO ($10); ReadyAI pay is flat — top $283/month, 10th-best percentile $234, median $194, 75th-from-top $181; ours $110/$109
(rank 236/248, still filling its EMA: α 0.1 per observation, reset on new hotkey, cubed after normalisation). Ceiling for a stock-quality slot ≈ the
median; the top of the field is only ≈ 1.45× it. Deployment of (1)+(2) awaits the user's OK (restarts r1/r2).

## §1193 — ReadyAI: validators grade with gpt-5.2; our miners moved from gpt-4o-mini to gpt-5.2 (central15 kept) (S11)

**No trial (lab + live change, user-approved).** Live read 00:00 UTC 10-31: r1/r2 ≈ $117/month at 7.6 h, near the bottom of their age cohort
(immune miners: median $129 at 6-9 h, $191 at 21-24 h); the lowest non-immune miner earns $172, so on that path immunity ends (≈ 16:40 UTC) near
the pruning line. Cause found in the code: on mainnet every validator is locked to the in-code default LLM (`llm_factory.configure_llm_override_lockdown`
→ `LlmOpenAI(ignore_model_override=True)`, DEFAULT_MODEL "gpt-5.2"), so the ground truth for every tag-similarity task (conversation tagging,
skill_generation, webpage metadata) is gpt-5.2's tags; our services set OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini. skill_generation gives the miner the same
1,000-character skill text the validator tagged (`SkillGenerationTaskBundle._generate_metadata`), so a default miner nearly reproduces the answer key.
Lab round 2 (`deploy/sn33/lab52.py`, 20 conversations × 2 windows, ground truth = gpt-5.2 on the full conversation, the evaluator's formula):
central15 on gpt-5.2 **+9.3% vs live** (cubed +30%, paired t 4.1); stock prompt on gpt-5.2 +1.5% (t 0.6); live central15 on mini = baseline; stock
on mini −8.2% (t −5.4). Our live setup ≈ a default miner on conversations; central15 was compensating for the weaker model. Deployed 00:45 UTC:
drop-in `readyai-rN.service.d/model.conf` OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5.2, central15 unchanged (skill and combine paths stay stock = the validator's own
pipeline). Wallet/W&B: validator per-UID scores go to W&B afterparty/conversationgenome, which is private (403). Cost of gpt-5.2 to be read from
the usage log. Earlier the same evening: stock miners busy-loop on sync() (§1192 fix live).

## §1195 — SN83 CliqueAI refresh: our solver now ties the best size on 93/98 live problems, but the field wins on answer diversity — parked (S11)

**No trial (measurement).** Chain: burn $24, median UID $521/month, top-10% ≥ $1,263, 25 operators (top 5 hold 84% of UIDs). Scoring
(CliqueAI v0.0.17 `scoring/clique_scoring.py`): reward = optimality·(1 + difficulty) + diversity, optimality = exp(−pr/rel) (pr = share of
responders strictly larger), diversity = 1 / (responders returning the identical clique); EMA α 0.01; weights min-max → sigmoid at the median.
98 newest logged problems (10-27, W&B toptensor-ai/CliqueAI, which also logs every responder's hotkey, coldkey and reward); our answer
inserted into the real responder set (`synth/clique_rank.py`). Single portfolio answer: 87/98 best size, diversity 0.61 vs field 0.85 → mean
reward 2.35, beats 2% of hotkeys (field median 2.64). A 200-step plateau walk moves cliques by ≈ 1 node and barely helps (2.353). 8 restarts,
least-frequently-found maximum clique (`deploy/sn83/multi_bench.py`, `portfolio.py`): 93/98 best size, optimality 0.974 (field 0.981), diversity
0.566 → 2.385, still 2nd percentile; 65% of our answers coincide with ≥ 1 logged answer. The maximum cliques share a large core, the field
already covers most of them, and big operators spread their many UIDs across distinct cliques; a newcomer's answer usually duplicates one.
Closing the gap needs full enumeration of each problem's maximum cliques to find unclaimed ones — parked. Live miner wrapper ready
(`deploy/sn83/our_miner.py`: one solve per graph per box, a different clique per UID).

## §1201 — SN33 ReadyAI: the missing ≈ 12% was timeouts — 28% of our conversation answers exceeded the validator's 12 s; fixed (not deployed)

**Lab.** Validators dispatch each task with `timeout=task.timeout` (12 s default; 24 s for skill coverage). Since the gpt-5.2 switch our
conversation_tagging answers took median 10.1 s, p90 12.9 s, and 21 of 74 (28%) exceeded 12 s — scored zero; other task types were well
inside their limits. Conversation tagging is ≈ 40% of tasks, so ≈ 11-12% of all tasks scored zero, matching the ≈ 12% shortfall (§1193,
§1200). Cause: central15's two sequential calls plus the stock code's sequential per-enrichment-line calls and combine (up to 6 calls).
`deploy/sn33/speed_lab.py` (12 logged live tasks, 2-6 enrichment lines): stock 9.2 s median / 11.1 s max; central15 as live 9.9 / 12.3;
low effort + priority tier 8.4 / 10.8; + enrichment calls in parallel 5.4 / 6.6 (0 of 12 over 10 s). Quality (`lab_low.py`, 20 fresh
conversations × 2 windows, gpt-5.2 ground truth): central15 low+priority 0.544 vs central15 default 0.536 (+1.5%, t 1.2) vs stock gpt-5.2
0.526 (−1.9%). The fix is in `deploy/sn33/central15.py` (low effort + priority for the tagging calls; ConversationTaggingTask.mine runs the
enrichment calls concurrently); tested on logged tasks: 4.4-5.5 s. ReadyAI stays closed (§1200) unless the user re-enters a slot with this fix.
**§1201 addendum (16:36 UTC):** user re-entered ReadyAI with the speed fix: hotkey r3 = UID 107 (port 8097, gpt-5.2, central15 low+priority,
parallel enrichment; unit `deploy/sn33/readyai-r3.service`). r1/r2 left to prune and auto-stop (§1200). Wallet topped up ≈ $50 (≈ 0.21 TAO).

## §1205 — SN50 Synth refresh: the model wins in calm markets and loses in volatile ones — no slot for now (S11)

**No trial (backtest).** Exact backtest (Synth API per-prompt CRPS of every miner + realized paths, our forecasts scored with the subnet's
code). Replaying the cached 10-day window (to ≈ 10-29) with today's code reproduces the earlier result: todg_12_36_c_ou20@0.95 share 0.64%
vs median UID 0.33% — pipeline sound. The last 5 days were ≈ 2× as volatile (CRPS scale 53-76 vs 29-33) and the same model falls BELOW
the median everywhere: Crypto-24h BTC 0.022% vs 0.177%, ETH 0.054% vs 0.072%, SOL 0.059% vs 0.061%, XRP 0.015% vs 0.051%; Crypto-1h BTC
0.155% vs 0.467%. Variant grid on BTC (decay of the EWMA level toward the 7-day level 3 h → 12 h / 24 h, scale 0.95 → 1.0, OU on/off):
best volatile-window share 0.074% (todg_12_144_c_ou20@1.0) — still far below the median — and every slower variant gives up most of the
calm-window edge (0.68% → 0.23-0.39%). The gap is structural (regime adaptation), not a parameter; a GARCH-style / regime-aware volatility
model validated on both windows is the next step if Synth is revisited. No registration (0.8 TAO).
**§1205 addendum (21:00 UTC):** GARCH-style per-path variance (`todv_<hl>_<L lookback>_<α>_<β>`, `s50_backtest.ensemble`: each path's variance
h' = (1−α−β)L² + α·e² + β·h in time-of-day-profile units, h₀ = the EWMA level², L = recent level) on BTC: volatile 5 days best 0.035%
(todv_12_288_0.05_0.94_c, CRPS 64.1 vs median 53.4) vs current 0.017%; calm 10 days 0.25-0.48% vs current 0.62% (median 0.33%). Volatility
dynamics are not the gap; next: per-prompt diagnosis (drift / a few big days / start-price timing).
**§1205 addendum 2 (21:25 UTC), per-prompt diagnosis (BTC, last 5 days, `rows_BTC_5.json`):** the price cache has no gaps; our start price
matches the validator's (mean |diff| 2-7 bp, max 37 bp); Synth's scoring code is unchanged since our copy. In RAW CRPS we are at the field
median every day (ratio 1.00-1.01 on 10-25…10-29, 1.03 on 10-30). The field sits within ≈ 1-3% raw CRPS; the per-prompt transform (cap at the
90th percentile, minus the best) and softmax β 0.15 turn that into a steep payout: ≈ 1-3% worse than the median → ≈ 0.1× median pay (this
window), a few % better → ≈ 2× (the calm window). Our model is a median-level forecaster with regime-dependent pay; no structural fault.
Expected value of a 0.8 TAO slot ≈ break-even at current accuracy — hold; revisit only with a consistent few-% CRPS improvement (e.g. order
book / funding inputs).

## §1206 — SN79 live: the bots that pick us off trade on visible order flow; an order-flow predictor beats ours out of sample (S11)

**Live analysis.** Books are independent (median cross-book correlation of 10 s returns +0.002; other books' last 5 s move → this book's next
30 s: IC +0.01), and the 5 s before a bot fill on our quote show no larger visible move than before a background fill (+0.45 vs +0.55 ticks),
so the bots neither use other books nor merely react faster. QuoteAgent now records per book per update the new bid / ask size, the size
placed within 2 ticks of the touch, and cancelled size (tape "of" lines, `orderflow.py`): near-touch new-order imbalance (5 s) has rank IC
+0.23 / +0.27 with the next 5 / 30 s move, above the taker flow we use (+0.25 / +0.18); before bot fills the 5 s taker flow in the bot's
direction is ≈ 3.7× that before background fills (+288 vs +78) and net order-flow imbalance is −0.39 vs +0.13. `fit_orderflow.py` (the live
features of QuoteAgent._predict + of_new / of_near / of_cancel), 18 sim min, fit on the first 75% by time, held-out 30 s IC +0.353 vs
the deployed model's +0.252 (top-bottom decile +12.1 ticks) → model30_of.json, live from 22:01 UTC (pull + join + cap + 20 units
unchanged), comparison at 23:35 UTC (/opt/mvtrx/live_compare6.txt).
**§1206 addendum (23:15 UTC):** live order-flow model (22:00-23:10 UTC, 17 sim min): our markouts −0.35 / −0.17 ticks at 30 / 60 s
(20-unit-cap tape −1.29 / −1.25; other miners +1.30 / +1.76); background-taker fills +1.01 (≈ the field); bot takers still 19% at −6.25;
max position 69 units. Pull threshold 2 → 1 tick live from 23:10 UTC (comparison 00:45 UTC). Each of our three live restarts today
(20:26, 21:55, 23:10 UTC) was followed by the validator's simulation clock stalling ≥ 10 min (axon re-published → our agent re-initialised
with a large catch-up state); live restarts are now kept to a minimum — variants go to the lab sim, one winner per (re)registration.

## §1207 — SN79 live: the post-restart "validator stalls" were our miner; fixed. Our answers are ~4× slower than the field's (S11)

**The stall was ours (corrects the §1206 addendum).** py-spy on the live miner 13 min after the 23:08 UTC restart: 99% CPU inside
`AgentEventHistory.append` (taos/im/protocol/events.py), not waiting on the validator. On restart the base agent reloads every order /
cancel / trade it ever logged to CSV (`load_event_history`: 1.49 M rows, 77 MB since 10-31 11:50 UTC), then the first state trims to the
60-min lookback by popping the dict's oldest key one at a time; CPython re-scans the deleted slots on every `next(iter(d))`, so the trim is
quadratic and grew with each restart. While it ran we answered nothing. Fix (`deploy/sn79/fix_trim.sh`, applied 23:22 UTC): the trim is one
linear dict rebuild, and the CSV directory was moved to /opt/mvtrx/csv_archive/. The miner answered its first state 20 s after restart.
Live restarts are cheap again; the "keep restarts minimal" rule from §1206 no longer applies.
**Speed.** Validators delay each miner's instructions by an exponential curve over the 3 s timeout (10 ms floor, 1 s cap; taos/im/validator/
delays.py): field median ≈ 0.06 s → 10.7 ms; ours ≈ 0.24 s logged decompress (p50 0.237, p90 0.364 s) and ≈ 0.9 s per state in total by
py-spy → ≈ 13-40 ms. Every miner that answers faster acts on the same state before us — a bot that sees our stale quote lifts it before our
cancel lands, consistent with the bots' 19% of fills at −6.25 ticks. Profile of a state: decompress 65% (mostly pydantic building every
book level's order list and the accounts), base-agent update + CSV logging 15%, QuoteAgent 19%. `--agent.params lazy_load=1` skips the
eager build (QuoteAgent reads only fields the Lazy* objects expose). Also: every instruction after a book's first gets +5-25 ms, so
QuoteAgent now cancels the side its prediction says is exposed first. Both go live after the pull=1.0 comparison at 00:45 UTC.
**§1207 addendum (23:50 UTC), speed measured on live states.** Three live requests captured passively (tcpdump on the axon port,
`pcap_req.py`) and replayed through QuoteAgent (`replay.py`, median of 15 runs): 128 books × 21 levels a side with ≈ 70 resting orders
inside the levels and ≈ 64 events per book → ≈ 9k orders + 8k events built as pydantic objects per state. Network is not the gap: 570 kB
requests arrive in 3-14 ms over a kept-alive connection from the validator (Chicago, 18.5 ms RTT); replies are ≈ 5 kB; our server time
is 290-390 ms per request. Dashboard (record:miner_call_time_avg_5m): ours 0.53 s, rank 249 / 256; field median 0.12 s, p10 0.06 s.
Replay per state: current 0.237 s (decompress 0.147 + agent 0.087); lean=1 0.183 s; lazy_load=1 alone BREAKS QuoteAgent (lazy cancel
events have no `side`; the per-book try/except swallowed it → 4 orders instead of 1038) — never deploy lazy_load without raw;
**raw=1 lean=1 lazy_load=1 0.080 s** (decompress 0.027 + agent 0.050), orders and tape byte-identical to the current setup. The 00:45 UTC
live test is therefore the full speed package (`switch_fast.sh`) — one variable (speed), behaviour verified identical; cancel_first
(param, default off) is a later test of its own.
**§1207 addendum 2 (00:50 UTC 11-01).** Comparison 7 (/opt/mvtrx/live_compare7.txt): pull 1.0 tick (23:22-00:45 UTC, 23 sim min) vs pull 2:
30 / 60 s markouts −0.42 / −0.73 vs −0.36 / −0.18 ticks (others +1.16 / +1.44); miner takers 20% of our fills at −5.68 vs 19% at −6.24 —
no gain: pulling earlier does not keep the bots off us, consistent with our cancels arriving after their orders. pull 1.0 kept so the next

## §1209 — SN79: we were optimizing the wrong number — the making pool pays on capped realized spread, where we sit near zero (S11)

**No trial (desk + public gauges).** The validator publishes ≈ 90 per-miner gauges (miner_gauges{miner_gauge_name=…} on the public Grafana).
UID 93 at 11:30 UTC 11-01 vs the field median: two-sided maker notional 13.4M (p90 11.0M), time at best 534k s (p90 200k), daily maker
volume 0.36M (0.19M) — top-decile making — but debeta_making_realized 0 / captured 0 / making_share 0 (median 42 / 140 / 0.0038), skill
−0.65 (+0.25), trading_score 0, incentive 0. Mechanism (taos/im/validator/debeta.py): making credit = Σ_book 2·min(buy, sell) captured
spread × markout_quality, quality = clamp(R / C, 0, 1); per maker fill c = (mid − p)·q at the fill, r = (mark 20 s of sim time later − p)·q
**capped to ±|c|**, R and C summed over all fills (making_basis = realized, making_horizon_s = 20). Pool = debeta_weight 1 × w_make 0.5 =
half of trading emission (SN79 miners ≈ $65k/month in total → ≈ $32k/month pool), split ∝ credit; the other half pays on directional
skill (ours negative). The cap removes the tail losses that dominated our markout means. `rc_quality.py` (mid-based approximation of the
print mark): our R/C fast −0.002, pull 1.0 +0.071, edge 2 +0.043, cancel_first +0.048, sticky −0.081, snap −0.137, snap+flow −0.046;
field median +0.15…+0.26. Our two-sided capture ≈ 280 (field median ≈ 85, p90 ≈ 250-320), so credit = capture × R/C: pull 1.0 → rank 87
/ 162, ≈ 0.4% of the pool ≈ $125/month; R/C 0.25 at our volume ≈ 1.3% ≈ $400-450/month. Objective changes from the unweighted 30 s
markout to R/C at 20 s (capped, capture-weighted — far less noisy). Arms readouts now include R/C per arm.
**§1209 addendum (21:35 UTC), CORRECTION — exact replica.** `making_exact.py` runs the validator's own accumulate_book_capture over each book's
full trade stream with the live dials (centred window 15 prints, realized horizon 20 s, min order size 0.25, fee weight 0.005, votes off,
taker legs removed), then markout_quality and the two-sided credit exactly as reward.making_basis_sums. The mid-based R/C above was wrong:
captured and realized are measured against a print-centred mid (W prints either side), not the quote mid. Exact: our quality is 0 on every
tape — fast C 9.0 / R −27.1, pull 1.0 19.8 / −18.8, edge 2 1.4 / −12.6, cancel_first 10.8 / −3.8, sticky and snap negative C, arms1 (all
four arms, first 30 min) C −0.3…3.5 / R −1.3…−4.1 → credit 0, matching the dashboard's 0; the field's quality median 0.38-0.50, captured
C median ≈ 20-28 (ours ≈ field median on pull 1.0). By class (pull 1.0 tape; other fills' maker id masked so they still print into the
mid): background-taken C 37.9 / R +4.5 → quality +0.12; bot-taken C −18.1 / R −23.0; fills ≤ 1.6 units C 13.1 / R +0.4 (+0.03), full-size
fills C 6.7 / R −19.1. Our background fills alone would be paid; bot fills (negative even at the fill) erase them. Arms readouts now use
making_exact per arm. Lever: cut bot / full-size fills, not average quality.

**Trial (lab, then live re-entry, user-approved 11-02 04:50 UTC).** r3 settled ≈ $120 vs a ≈ $161 pruning line after the gpt-5.2 and speed
fixes (§1200-§1201). Pay = EMA of absolute per-task scores, normalized and cubed, so +10% raw ≈ +33% pay. Read against the validator code:
(1) conversation_tagging scores each tag by cosine to the MEAN embedding of the ground-truth tags (gpt-5.2 on the FULL conversation +
gpt-5.2 tags of each enrichment snippet, combined); 0.55·top-3 unique + 0.25 mean + 0.10 median + 0.10 max; validate_tag_set keeps a
tag only if its cleaned form (Utils.get_safe_tag) equals a tag we sent, so punctuated tags ("end-to-end testing") were silently dropped
(10% of ours; 8% on skill_generation), and ≥ 20 tags are randomly sampled to 20. `lab_final.py` (20 conversations × 2 windows,
synthesized enrichment, the repo's own LlmLib on gpt-5.2, scored after validate_tag_set): live 0.522; pre-cleaned +2.2% (t 0.8);
pre-cleaned + 12 nearest own centroid **+3.9%** (t 1.8); 6-8 tags −2%, 4 tags −24% (unique top-3 starves). (2) skill_coverage
(36% of tasks): section score = mean of the top-2 judged-correct tests' cosine to the embedding of "{title}: {description}" — text the
miner receives — with 3 random sections scored, too_few_tests (< 5 over those 3) ×0.5, near-duplicate (any pair ≥ 0.95) ×0.5, and an
LLM judge on assertions only. `sc_headroom.py`: live section coverage 0.554 vs 0.890 with the section text as description.
`sc_lab2.py` (all 47 logged r3 tasks through format_results + the scoring mechanism, real gpt-5.2 judge, paired sections): live 0.395
(19% zeros: judge failed every assertion), anchored **0.542 (+37%, t 4.4)**, anchored + self-judge **0.575 (+46%, t 4.9)**.
Task-mix weighted ≈ +13-15% raw → ≈ +44-53% pay → r3 ≈ $175-185 vs the $161 line. Patch `deploy/sn33/scoring_fixes.py`
(imported by run_miner.py after central15): tagging pre-clean + trim to 12; skill_generation pre-clean; skill coverage anchor (test 2
nearest the section with cosine to test 1 < 0.94) + our own judge pass at low effort / priority (≈ 5 s; abandoned at 21 s of the 24 s
limit). Timing: generation ≈ 8 s + anchor ≈ 2 s + judge ≈ 5 s. run_miner.py logs time-to-answer (dt). Re-entry: hotkey r3 (SN33 burn

pace; x2 reached $321k on its hottest book in ≈ 30 sim min. Fixes, all replay-identical when off: books split between UIDs (x1:

UIDs never trade with each other); max_units 40 → 100 (one $30-book order is ≈ 100 units); `fit_qty` (quote the affordable part);
`pace_cap` / `pace_win` / `pace_k`: quote a book only while our trailing-24-sim-h notional < pace_cap (450k) and the trailing 90-sim-min
