- Validator (reward.py allocate_trading): making is paid PROPORTIONALLY to captured-spread credit; skill is paid on a Pareto ladder with a
  soft floor at the median of positive skill (tapered to 0 below). Newcomer EMA: standing tracks live performance (alpha = 1/(k+1)).
  Check: emission score ≈ 4.5e-6 × making credit (x2 230 → 0.0010; x1 700 → 0.0033). Prune floor ≈ 0.0015.
- x2 pruned 11-04 18:52 UTC: the book SPLIT left x2 on low-volume calm books (~230 credit) and x1 on volatile books (~0 credit), so both were weak.
  Multi-UID owners (41/16/15/13/12 UIDs) stack every UID on the SAME books (124-127 of 128 overlap) and each earns 165-420 credit,
  because the volume cap is per UID per book. A stacked second UID needs all taking off on both (no self-trades).
- Two owners (10 UIDs each) get the TOP scores with zero making credit, from skill alone. Top-20 live-skill UIDs: pure takers, ~$1k clips, 40-90 books.
  They trade AGAINST the prior 60 s move 70% of the time and ignore the fundamental gap (52%) and order flow (49%). Mid moves their way
  +2.1 bp at 10 s (74% hit) and +2.0 bp at 15 min. skill_val replica: positive for 114/238/120 with kept counts similar to the gauges.
- Naive 60-s fade backtest (mid-to-mid, no own impact): +0.3 to +1.2 bp/notional median per book, few books past the 2.3 bp hurdle.
  The top UIDs reach +1.3 to +3.1, so either better timing or own impact (which the validator counts). This is decided live.
- LIVE TEST on x1 from 19:37 UTC: rev_look=60 rev_hold=180 rev_usd=1000 sleeve_bp=4 sleeve_step=20 on 40 books (skip_x1 = sleeve_books_x1),
  making on the other 88. Backups: QuoteAgent.pre-rev.py, skip_x1.pre-rev.txt, sleeve_books_x1.pre-rev.txt, tape.conf.pre-rev.
  Replay check: rev off identical to live (926 instructions), rev on only IOC on the sleeve books.
- §1223 add. 1 (20:38 UTC): top-taker rules from 36,100 trades: hold median 630 s (p75 1,440), fade signal strongest at 300 s lookback
  (68% against; median prior move 2.9 bp), clip median $1,013, own impact only +0.34 bp then drift +1.65 bp (64% hit). They mostly trade the
  calm ~$30 books (spread 6.8 bp). x1 test switched to rev_look=300 rev_hold=600 sleeve_bp=3 on the same 40 books (backup tape.conf.rev60).

  trading with each other: taker writes lock_<book>_<maker side>, maker pulls that side and writes ack only once its account shows no order

## §1224 — SN82 Noah deep dive (2026-11-04 evening, user asked): a capital-for-yield loop, not mining; parked until MVTRX earnings exist (S11)
- Repo Vora-Inc/NOAH (fa9c0c2, 11-04): no miner software or GPU. Pay = √(age-decayed NOAH contribution credit) × multiplier, where multiplier =
  min((PCI/0.5)², 2) and PCI = contributions / spendable earnings. Contributions to the Ark (coldkey 5EL1nNeb…, delegated to hotkey 5DLQGc9D…)
  are PERMANENT, and 50% of all earnings must keep flowing back. Starter entry (from 11-03) gives ~5 NOAH per coldkey, lifetime, from a 0.25% pool.
- Chain 11-04: miner pool 1,282 NOAH/day ≈ $350k/month (NOAH 0.0387 TAO, TAO $235). 30 paid UIDs, 45-50 NOAH/day each; two coldkeys
  (12 and 11 UIDs) take ~85%. Ark holds 53,436 NOAH ≈ $486k. Burn 8.4 TAO ≈ $2k per UID.
- Rough estimate (assumes ~1,700 credit per established UID): 100 NOAH in → ~11 NOAH/day, net ~5.5 after paybacks (≈ $1.5k/month), upfront ≈ $2.9k,
  payback ~2 months; 400 in → net ≈ $3k/month for ≈ $5.6k. Risks: NOAH has no use outside the loop (price rests on contributors; the two big wallets
  earn ~$300k/month); contributions are lost; the credit level isn't verified (needs a scan of all receipts). Earlier memory of "needs a GPU" was wrong.
- §1223 add. 5 (01:00 UTC 11-05): x2 (UID 169) crashed 2,214 times/hour in _record (tape writer): its event stream delivers pydantic
  Cancellation objects with no .side, so respond_simulation aborted and sent NO orders on those steps (x1 unaffected). Fix: x2 tape off (x1's
  tape has every trade), getattr guard in _record. x2 restarted 00:59 UTC, 0 errors after. x2's live skill read before this is understated.
- §1223 add. 6 (01:07 UTC 11-05): x1 (UID 213) PRUNED. Its service is stopped. x2's lock handshake is off (no maker left to ack). An x2 tape
  re-enable crashed in the framework's lazy loader ('list' object has no attribute 'get', 18 in 2 min), so x2 runs with no tape; an

## §1229 — Synth tail check: our 24 h forecasts are calibrated on average; the big-move-day loss is not a fixable width error (2026-11-05 04:05 UTC) (S11)

  fast todg_12_36_c_ou20@0.95 and slow todg_12_144_c_ou20@1.0.

- Big-move third: 24 h tail hits 25-36%, |move|/sd ≈ 1.2-1.5. That's expected when conditioning on the realized move (any calibrated
  forecast shows it), so it is not evidence of narrow tails. Widening would cost the other two thirds; IV scaling (§1211) didn't help.
- Read: Synth's big-move losses come from moves that aren't predictable from price history at prompt time. No width fix; at most a small SOL narrowing (k ≈ 0.9) to test in the forward run.

## §1231 — SN67 Harnyx deep look: submit a research agent; ~40 "main participants" earn ≈ $590/month each; offline eval built in (2026-11-05 04:40 UTC) (S11)

  tool proxy, billed to the MINER's own provider keys; per-task session budget $0.50). Validators run it in a sandbox on a DAILY batch
  (cutoff 15:00 UTC): 10 qualifying + 20 main tasks; score = F1 vs a stronger reference answer + a pairwise judge (Overall = 0.3 F1 + 0.7 judge).

  40 main participants at 1.067% ≈ $591/month each; ~70 more at $39-236; ~160 get $0. Participant weight = stage (top 50% 1 / top 10% 2 /
  main 5) × novelty (near_duplicate 1 / notable_change 3 / novel 10). Exact duplicates get nothing. Chain: pool ≈ $55k/month, burn 0.072 TAO.
- Main round: up to 30 per title (F1, Overall) must pass the dethroning comparison against the incumbent on the 10 qualifying tasks:
  beat it by 10 points, OR match its score ≥ 10% cheaper, OR ≥ 10% and ≥ 1 s faster. Then rank by qualifying score, cost, runtime.

  via OpenRouter, writer deepseek-v4.1-flash), adjudicator, quoted-passage answers; stops at $0.27/task. ~275 artifacts/day.

  and a search key (champion uses Parallel; Desearch/Exa/Tavily/Firecrawl also supported).
- Economics per UID at the main tier: ≈ $591 − model/search spend (≈ $0.27 × 30 tasks ≈ $8/day ≈ $240/month at the champion's spend;
  ≈ $3/day if it only qualifies) → net ≈ $350/month; a notable/novel change ×3/×10. Next: reproduce the champion locally, then a ≥ 10%-cheaper,
  equal-score variant (main-tier entry) and real improvements (novelty / title).

## §1233 — MVTRX reversal predictor: a real raw edge on an unseen slice (2026-11-05 06:20 UTC) (S11)
- predfeat.py: every 5 sim s per book: Δmid 1/5/30/60/300 s, Δfund 1/10/60 s, gap (fund−mid) and its 10 s change, top-5 depth imbalance,
  spread, other takers' signed flow 10 s, new-minus-cancelled book flow 10 s, big trades 5 s; targets: mid move 60 s / 600 s (bp).
  TRAIN = x1 tape slice ending 1,800 MB back (252,928 rows); TEST = latest 850 MB (254,976 rows), unseen.
- predfit.py, ridge on z-scores: test corr +0.25 (60 s) / +0.17 (600 s), above in-sample (+0.20 / +0.12). Weights (600 s, per sd): depth imbalance
  +0.66, Δfund 60 s +0.48, Δmid 60 s −0.41, gap −0.24, spread +0.24, flow +0.24, gap change +0.20.
- Trading sim on TEST (one bet per book per hour, 600 s hold, mid-to-mid): S5 +0.97 bp / 57% hit, books pass 23% fail 9% |
  model top 2% |forecast| +4.24 bp / 72%, 95 books pass 42% fail 5% | top 0.5% +5.95 bp / 76%, 53 books pass 53% fail 6%.
- Next: a second unseen slice (ending 900 MB back), then a live implementation + replay check. Live test after x2's V0 verdict (or on a new UID).
  Remember §1199: an offline-fit predictor was backwards live.
- §1233 add. 1 (07:00 UTC): second unseen slice (ending 900 MB back) confirms: corr +0.22 / +0.17; top 2% +5.30 bp, 67% hit, books pass 47% fail 7%;
  top 0.5% +7.23 bp, 72%; S5 +0.62 bp. Model exported (predexport.py → agents/rev_model.json, threshold |forecast| ≥ 3.19 bp = top 2% of train).
  Live features in revfeat.py, shared with revfeat_parity.py: replaying the tape through the live code reproduces the training forecast at
  corr 0.997, 1,919 vs 1,907 entries, 1,872 identical. Bugs found and fixed on the way: trades filed under the snapshot second (dropped),
  flow means folded before the second's trades (always 0), flow scale before warm-up (exploded) → 600 s warm-up.

## §1244 — Skill side (2026-11-05, 10:10 PM CT): the top skill miners' score is not trading profit

Same 200 MB tape slice (38 sim min), x1 (114) vs ten top skill-only UIDs (skill gauge 3–4.3, $430–740/month).

**Behaviour (skillcmp.py).** All are pure takers: ~1,250–1,500 fills per 38 sim min, median fill $490–1,000, 62–86 books, mean |inventory|
about $130–170k, round trip about 320–610 s, notional $1.8–3.5M/h. Their fills' mid markouts are negative at 30, 120 and 600 s (about −0.7 to
−2.7 bp; UID 48 is the exception at +1.5 to +2.1). x1: 267 fills, median $268, mean |inv| $3.6k, notional $0.14M/h (15× less).

**Score (skill_val.py, validator formula).** Top UIDs: 44–71 books kept by the hurdle, almost all positive (UID 8: 64 of 64), α/notional median
+3.1 to +3.9 bp, kappa +2.2 to +4.5. x1: 45 kept (26 positive, 19 negative), +0.42 bp, kappa +0.28.

**Decomposition (skill_decomp.py).** The scorer's alpha is Σ inventory × Δmid − mean inventory × drift. It never charges the fill price.

| uid | alpha bp | own impact (first mid move after own print) | rest of holding | drift adjustment | true P&L at fill prices |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | +4.18 | +1.20 | +1.41 | +1.57 | −0.41 |
| 103 | +7.25 | +1.87 | +3.62 | +1.76 | −2.39 |
| 48 | +5.12 | +1.08 | +3.83 | +0.21 | +1.56 |
| 181 | +4.16 | +0.52 | +1.97 | +1.66 | −0.64 |
| 114 (x1) | +0.56 | +0.10 | +0.51 | −0.00 | −0.53 |

**Reading.** The top skill miners mostly score high while losing money at fill prices (3 of 4 checked). The score comes from three parts:
1. the mid moving after their own taking (their own impact);
2. holding sizeable inventory while the mid moves their way;
3. the drift adjustment, which is positive when mean inventory leans against the book's drift over the window.

x1 is small on all three because its size and inventory are about 40× smaller. A better predictor is not the main lever. Scale is: bigger
fills, real inventory held for minutes, and a lean against the drift.

**Caveats.**
- 38 sim min, scored from inventory 0; the validator's window and starting state differ.
- Unknown whether a sim-account drawdown from negative P&L is penalised.
- The subnet owner could patch the scorer to charge fill prices, so this is not durable by design.

**Next step:** an offline replay of x1's taker with 3–5× size and longer holds through skill_val.py before tomorrow's x1 registration.
Live is the only true test. Our UIDs must still never trade each other (the handshake covers it).

## §1246 — Pace ledger: a restart no longer forgets volume under the turnover cap (2026-11-05, 10:30 PM CT)

The user asked whether we could hit the volume cap again. Gap found: the pace was seeded only from the live tape, which holds about 20 wall
hours. The validator's window is 24 sim h, about 5 wall days. So every restart forgot most of the volume that counts toward the cap. With a
miner that runs for days and gets restarted for tests, this would have hit the cap again. The tape's .prev file was never read either.

**Fix: `pace_ledger=<path>`.** Our own fills are appended live (book, sim sec, notional, id, ts) and loaded at start, de-duplicated against
the tape seed. Details:
- "UIDN" in the path becomes our UID, because the cap is per UID and a re-registered hotkey starts clean.
- At the first step, and whenever the sim clock goes backwards (a new simulation), stored times shift so the newest sits at the current
  step. This is conservative: the volume is kept, and no gap is assumed.

Tests:
- Without the param, the replay is identical to the live agent.
- A ledger with 64 books at $460k and a far-future clock is loaded and shifted; 64 of 64 of those books are paced out and 0 of the other 64.
- The UIDN path resolves (replay uid 93 → /tmp/pace_93.ledger).

The agent is installed; running x1 and x3 keep their loaded code. add_skill_uid.sh has a new **M1S** variant (the §1245 scaled taker:
take_size 60, rev_usd 5000, rev_th_k 0.7, pace 450k/5400, pace_ledger=/opt/mvtrx/pace_UIDN.ledger). x3 gets
`pace_ledger=/opt/mvtrx/pace_UIDN.ledger` at its next restart, after the §1242 A/B verdict.

**Still open.** The pace budget (≈ $18.75k per book per sim hour) is below the top skill UIDs' observed $22–40k (§1244). Their wealth may be
higher, or they may run into the cap themselves. If §1245 shows the score scales with size, the remaining room is more books per UID, not
more per book.

## §1247 — x3 bad books, scaling capacity, and a lab test of what skill rewards (2026-11-05, 10:55 PM CT)

**#1 x3's bad books (making_exact_dump.py --books, 500 MB slice, x3 = 58).**
- Over the whole slice: quality 0.322. Dropping the 30 worst-R books (in-sample) gives 0.449 with C 882 → 860.
- Large fills carry almost all of it (C 859 of 882); small fills are irrelevant; bot-taken C 302 at 0.335.
- **Out of sample** (worst books picked on the first half, scored on the second): 0.330 → 0.358 / 0.365 / 0.367 / 0.375 for 10/20/30/40
  dropped, vs random drops of the same size at median 0.33 and p95 0.35–0.38. **Individual books do not hold.**
- The **regime** holds in both halves. Volatile ids 0–62: quality −0.54 / −0.02. Calm 63–101: +0.54 / +0.47. 4-decimal 102–127: +0.14 / +0.41.
  Without the volatile group, quality would be 0.50 / 0.46. Rough credit effect (C kept × quality): +28% / +2%.
- New `mk_skip_vol=1` (no making on books 0–62). Replay with x3's params: off identical (517 placements); `arms=mk_skip_vol:1` gives the odd
  volatile books 0 placements and leaves the even ones (115) and calm/4-dec (297) quoting. The agent is installed; running miners keep
  their loaded code.
- Proposed next x3 test, after the §1242 verdict: arms=mk_skip_vol:1 (book mod 2), read per arm with making_exact after ≥ 45 sim min.

**#2 Scaling capacity (lab box, measured).**
- Per miner: ≈ 320 MB RAM (process tree), 6–13% of one core, ≈ 120 KB/s inbound. Inbound is free on DO; outbound 2 KB/s.
- One 4 vCPU / 8 GB box ($48/month) fits ≈ 12–15 miners with headroom for analysis, so ≈ $3–4 per miner-month.
- Registration burn 0.113 TAO now (≈ $23). SN79 targets 1 registration per 360 blocks (72 min) subnet-wide, and the burn rises with
  demand, so our own registrations push it up. Immunity is 7,200 blocks; there are 256 slots.
- **Constraint:** the no-self-trade handshake (lock_dir) is files on one box, so all our makers and takers must share one box, or the
  lock must become networked. One larger box (8 vCPU / 16 GB ≈ $96) would hold ≈ 30.
- **Unknown, and the real scaling test:** whether a second UID running the same strategy on the same books cannibalizes the first. Makers
  compete for the same takers, and their credit comes from one pool; takers take the same liquidity. Each UID gets its own volume cap.
- Rough path to $10k: ≈ 40 UIDs × $250. Cost ≈ $1k of burns plus ≈ $150–200/month of boxes, before re-registrations.

**#3 Lab: does skill reward direction, or size and impact?** The lab sim publishes no fundamental ("fund": null), so the fitted model
cannot trade there (no forecast). Instead the rule-based reversal (rev_look 300, sleeve_bp 8, hold 900, step 900, $5k, take 60) runs as
three agents in one market: real direction (agent 0), random (1, `rev_rand=1`), opposite (2, `rev_rand=2`). Same timing and size, scored
with skill_val + skill_decomp. Three runs (seeds 1–3, ≈ 25 wall min each) via /opt/mvtrx/labrand_runner.sh →
/opt/mvtrx/labrand_scores.txt. The scorer's alpha equals Σ (inventory − its mean) × Δmid, so §1244's "drift adjustment" is not a separate
source; that correction is noted here.

## §1249 — The top skill miners run our kind of strategy; the difference is how often they re-enter (2026-11-06, ≈ 6:00 AM CT)

**Clone (clone.py).** Train: x1's tape, 600 MB ending 250 MB before its end. Test: x3's own tape, last 400 MB; independent, later.
- Entries (taker trades that grow |inventory|) of the ten top skill-only UIDs: 23,705 train / 8,396 test joined to our 15 features.
- A ridge-logistic clone predicts **their direction with 85.4% accuracy on test** (train 83.2%, base 51.2%). Per UID 0.78–0.92, except UID 48
  at 0.52, which runs something else.
- The dominant weight is dmid300 (z −2.5), then dfund60 −0.8 and dmid60 −0.8: **they fade the last 5 minutes**, as v1 does. v1 agrees with
  their direction on 63% of test entries.
- Their entries are right by +1.53 / +1.51 / +1.34 / +0.55 bp at 300 / 600 / 900 / 1800 s, so their hold is ≈ 5–10 min, matching the
  320–610 s round trips in §1244.

**Paper skill (validator hurdle_filter 2.3 bp + kappa_floored; no own impact, no spread; one position per book, re-entry right after the
hold). Test slice:**
- random ≈ 0 everywhere, so the scorer is sane.
- **v1 beats the clone** at every setting. Best v1: q 0.05 with H 300–900 → kappa 5.7–6.0, 16–17 kept, all positive. The clone's best is
  1.8.
- Imitating them does not beat our model; v1's direction is better than the clone's.

**Calibration (same training slice, the M1 live period).**
- Paper v1 at x1's settings (q 0.02, H 900): 25 kept / 24 positive, median +1.78 bp, kappa +1.11.
- The validator formula on x1's real fills: 17 kept / 12 positive, median +0.55 bp, kappa +0.41.
- **The paper scorer is optimistic by ≈ 2–3×**, the same direction as v1's offline-to-live shrink (≈ half). Use it for ranking only, never
  for levels. Part of the gap is structural: live M1 re-enters a book at most once per sim hour (sleeve_step 3600), while the paper
  re-enters after each hold.

**Threshold.** v1's threshold 3.19 is now the top 5% of |forecast| on both slices (forecast scale drifted), so live x1 already trades
≈ q 0.05.

**What differs from the top UIDs** is entry spacing. They are in a position almost continuously: ≈ 1,300 entries per 38 sim min over ≈ 80
books. M1 bets once per book per sim hour. The §1245 scaled test kept sleeve_step 3600, so "more entries" was never tested; it changed size
and threshold.

**Proposal for the new x1:** M1 at normal size plus `arms=sleeve_step:900` (re-enter after each 900-s hold on odd books; even books stay
on M1 at 3600), read per arm with skill_val on book subsets. Arms are generic attribute overrides in _quote, so this works on the taker
path. Correction (same session): the paper scorer always re-enters after the hold, so it has NOT tested M1's once-per-hour spacing against step = hold. The spacing lever is a hypothesis from the top UIDs' behaviour, not a paper result. The live A/B decides.

**§1249 add. 1 (≈ 6:00 AM CT): paper test of entry spacing, inconclusive.** v1 at th 3.19, hold 900, minimum gap between entries per book
3600 / 1800 / 900 s:
- Train slice: kappa 2.76 / 4.19 / 6.48 (kept 38 / 36 / 26, nearly all positive).
- Test slice: 0.98 / 0.85 / 0.56 (kept 17 / 17 / 13).

The two independent slices disagree on direction, so the paper gives no reliable evidence that faster re-entry helps. kappa also jumps when
fewer books are kept and all are positive, which makes it a noisy ranking metric on 1–2 sim-h slices.

**Decision for the new x1:** plain M1 (proven live: skill 0.58) with pace_ledger. Spacing is tested only as a live arm, and only after the
new x1 is established above the prune line, so the test cannot cost its survival.

**Housekeeping (2026-11-06 6:25 AM CT):** stopped three leftover transient timers: mvtrx-window-est (UID 213, the 11-02 size test on
live_tape_x1_size6), mvtrx-window-est-x2 (UID 247) and mvtrx-skillread. They had kept scoring dead UIDs every hour; the running
making_exact (PID 436079) used ≈ 3 GB on x3's box and was killed by exact PID. Free memory went from 4.2 to 6.8 GB. x3 was unaffected.

| field median (> $0.1M) | | 133 (p75 187, p90 218) | | 0.67 | | |

## §1252 — Top makers run a depth ladder; x3 only sits at the touch (2026-11-06, 10:36 AM CT)

**quotemap.py** (x3 tape, sim min 1159 on): every maker fill against the last book snapshot.

| uid | at touch | deeper | inside | dist from mid, median (mean) bp | dist / spread p50 / p75 / p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 58 (x3) | 91% | 9% | 0% | 1.00 (1.52) | 0.50 / 0.50 / 0.50 |
| 144 | 36% | 50% | 15% | 3.31 (4.61) | 0.50 / 1.30 / 3.28 |
| 252 | 31% | 52% | 17% | 3.33 (5.02) | 0.64 / 1.50 / 3.50 |
| 31 | 32% | 51% | 16% | 3.38 (4.93) | 0.61 / 1.50 / 3.50 |
| 7 | 33% | 52% | 15% | 3.38 (5.52) | 0.60 / 1.49 / 3.50 |
| 42 | 53% | 17% | 30% | 0.67 (1.38) | 0.50 / 0.50 / 0.75 (small $145 fills) |

Calm books: x3 3.3 bp from the mid, the template makers 6.7 bp. $150+ books: x3 0.67, the template 1.35–1.5 (mean 3.2–4.2). The percentiles
fall on 0.5 / 1.5 / 3.5 spreads, which suggests **a ladder of resting orders**, not one wider quote (inferred from fills, not observed
directly): sweeps reach the deep levels, which keep far more spread. The earlier x3 study already showed fills near the touch give up most
of the spread.

**Built `mk_lad1` / `mk_lad2`:** extra post-only orders that many spreads from the mid, rounded outward, on each side still wanted. Every pull
above them (thin rule, flow pull, lock handshake) removes them, so the self-trade rule still holds. Replay: off identical (184 placements);
on 778 placements, all post-only, no errors. Ladders reprice with the mid, so instruction volume is ≈ 4×. Replaces the planned bp width.

**Live:** x3 restarted 16:35:27 UTC (10:35 AM CT, sim min ≈ 1224), pre-approved param test: arms=edge:3/mk_lad1:1.5+mk_lad2:3.5 (book mod 3).
The edge:6 arm, 9 minutes old, was replaced. Backup mvtrx-x3.service.pre-lad, agent QuoteAgent.pre-lad.py. First minute: 0 errors, 0
self-trades. Full verdict needs ≥ 45 sim min (≈ 2:20 PM CT); x3 may be pruned first. Risk: deep fills come from sweeps and can carry
inventory and adverse selection, so judge quality as well as credit.

**§1252 add. 1 (2026-11-06, 11:20 AM CT): x3 was fully paced out; the ladder had no data.** x3 made zero fills from its 10:35 AM restart to
11:19 AM (last fill sim s 73,049). All 39 calm and 26 4-decimal books were over the 90-sim-min limit ($28,125; recent medians $29,441 and
$28,758), and x3 no longer quotes the other 63. The clue: MK QUALITY showed 13,021 decisions and 0 thin sides pulled, because the only
unpaced books were the volatile ones, where want is already empty. They would have come back at ≈ sim min 1248–1259 (≈ 12:50 PM CT), likely
after pruning. Earlier "credit is flat" reads hid this.

**Fix:** pace_k=2 (90-min limit $56,250), restart 17:19:58 UTC (11:20 AM CT, sim min 1232). The 24-sim-h cap of $450k stays (≈ $250k used per
book). Backup mvtrx-x3.service.pre-pacek. Fills resumed within a minute. A/B data now starts at sim min 1232; full verdict ≈ 3:05 PM CT.

**Design lesson:** the rolling 90-sim-min window (7.5 wall h) is stop-go, not even spending. x3 spends the allowance in a burst, then idles for
hours; last night's 4-hour gap was the same thing. A replacement maker needs a much shorter pace window or smaller, steadier quoting, or it
will sit out most of each window.

## §1255 — Volume pacing rebuilt: a token bucket, the validator's own figure, and a standing watchdog (2026-11-06, 3:30 PM CT)

The user: pacing has failed too many times; hitting the cap must never be an issue again; fix it before registering a new maker.

**The rule, from the validator's code (repo at published head 9133060):** query.py drops every non-cancel instruction on a book when volume_sums ≥ capital_turnover_cap (10)
× miner_wealth. volume_sums = maker + taker + self notional per UID per book, over trade_volume_assessment_period (86,400 sim s), sampled at 600 s. A sim boundary SHIFTS the
timestamps and keeps the volume (my notes implied a reset). Only deregistration clears it (reset_agent_histories). "accrued for a new uid" is dead code. miner_wealth is per book.
Live confirmation: 1,751 book/UID pairs across the field at ≥ $490k, top $527k. x3 was never dropped (public `dropped` gauge 0).

**How pacing failed:** none at first (11-03); taker path unpaced; restart forgot history; x3 had no tape to seed from and ran 5× fast for 11 h unnoticed; previous owner's fills seeded in;
the 90-sim-min window was stop-go by design; I loosened it by hand with pace_k; and 44 minutes of zero fills went unseen.

**Rebuilt (QuoteAgent.py):**
- **Token bucket per book** replaces the rolling window: earns pace_cap / 86,400 ($5.21 per sim s), holds 900 sim s at most, fills spend it, and it may go negative. Quoting or opening
  needs a positive balance; exits still go. Long-run rate is exact whatever the fills, so 24 h ≤ $450k + burst $4.7k + one order set. The 24-h sum stays as a backstop.
- **No override:** pace_win and pace_k are ignored, with a warning. Removed from the setup scripts.
- **Ledger is the record** (tape seed off when a ledger exists). Replay through the bucket at start, so a restart resumes the same balance. A sim reset no longer corrupts it.
- **PACE STATUS** every sim minute: books blocked, 24-h median and max, and the validator figure.
- **Account.traded_volume arrives as None** in the state we receive, so it is unusable. **Public `agent_gauges{daily_volume}` per book is the validator's figure.** On x1 it matches the
  ledger (book 123 $7,756 both after sync; the ledger leads by the gauge's lag), so the ledger errs safe. Two sim_ids report; we trade one (the other reads 0).
- **pace_sync.py** (every 10 min): writes that figure to pace_sync_<uid>.json. The agent charges any excess over $1,000 once, into the ledger too. This covers fills missed during
  restarts. Agents read it once per sim minute.
- **Watchdog is now standing** (overnight.sh): registration of every UID in our_uids.txt, sync, and ALERT lines to alerts.txt for: not registered, ≥ 90% of the cap, any dropped
  instruction, no fills (45 min maker, 180 min taker).
- Setup scripts archive any old ledger for a re-used UID.

**Tests (test_pace.py, the agent's real methods, all pass):** filled whenever open for 3 sim days: worst 24 h $454,952 ($3k orders), $466,633 ($10k), $493,153 (one $50k sweep each
time), all under $500k. Longest idle on one book 1,688 sim s ($3k orders) vs 5,396 for the old window. $450,003 of budget usable in a day. Restart same balance; restart cannot reopen a
spent book; sim reset gives no free budget; restart after a sim reset keeps all volume; pace_k cannot loosen it; validator charge applied once and survives restart. Replay: identical
to the prior agent with x1's and a maker's params when not bound (120, 184 placements).

**Known limits:** the bucket bounds volume, not earnings; order size sets the gaps ($3k orders can idle ≈ 28 sim min on a book at the limit, so smaller orders run steadier). The public
gauge lags, and if the endpoint fails the watchdog alerts rather than blocks. The sync protects one sim only.

**§1255 end-to-end lab result (2026-11-06, 3:53 PM CT):** a real maker with real fills, 70 sim min on 16 books. Paced by the bucket: 205 fills, $24,137 per book (max $25,521), bound
$32,562, 0 books over it; longest gap between fills on a book 587–704 sim s, so it traded steadily. Identical unpaced control: 14,328 fills, $1,141,187 per book (max $1,675,606), which
would pass the $500k cap in about 30 sim minutes. The 2 tracebacks were the background Random agents at sim shutdown, not ours.

**Pacing: go.** Replacement maker prepared on the x3 unit (backup .pre-new): size 0.036 (the top makers' ≈ $1,800 orders, steadier under the bucket), pace_cap 450000, ledger, mk_skip_vol=1,
mk_thin_ratio 0.77, arms=back:1/back:2. Old ledger and tape archived. Not started; waits for the user's registration.

**§1255 add. 1 (2026-11-06, 4:00 PM CT): pre-registration checks, one old bug found.**

  equal across groups; ids 0–62 are the $300, 2-decimal books. Spreads 2.3 bp ($300), 6.75 ($30), 3.5 (4-dec).
- **model30_of (10-31) is in dollars, not ticks.** On recent tape: corr +0.08 on the books we quote, top decile +0.2–0.3 bp, −0.7 on the $300 books. Its median forecast is $0.008–0.018 on every

FAQ, README and code contain no written ban, but the scorer is built against it: debeta.py calls it a "feeder ring"; P11 (p11_strength default 1.0) "removes the making credit of a maker
served by a dedicated taker", and skill_p11_strength applies a matching factor to skill. Capture is zero-sum per fill, so the maker's gain is the taker's cost. Top makers' p11 factor is 0.96–0.98: their miner flow comes from many takers. The no-self-trade rule stands.

**Coverage rule found in the FAQ:** skill is scaled by min(1, books filled / (0.625 × 128 = 80)). rev_skip_vol leaves x1 at 65 books once the earlier volatile fills age out of the window: factor ≈ 0.81 (gauge 1.0 today, 121 books still counted). The volatile filter has a cost that §1253 missed; the next x1 should keep ≥ 80 books.

## §1259 — Top takers use no stop-loss; a wider target reproduces their score pattern on paper (2026-11-06, 6:53 PM CT)

The user asked whether top takers use stops. **No fixed stop visible.** Closed losers are small and few (median −1.7 to −3.5 bp, worst −8 to −28), but open positions sit at −30 to −93 bp, dips reach −864 bp on positions still open, and 8–20% of positions go past −10 bp, 2–6% past −20. Closed winners had dipped −4 to −7 bp (p10), up to −150. Losers are held much longer than winners on most UIDs (e.g. 2,766 vs 562 s).
They wait; the small closed "losers" look like scratches, not stops.

**Hypothesis tested (parked.py, walk-forward, scorer's alpha on the 5-s mid path; one position per book; fit chunk 3 → test 4 / fit 2 → test 3; all books):**

| exit | kept / positive | median α bp | total α | raw P&L |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| clock 900 s (x1 today) | 55/55, 45/41 | +2.18, +1.43 | +2.95, +1.61 | +3.00, +1.89 |
| target 2 bp | 29/29, 15/15 | +1.70, +1.56 | +2.10, +2.00 | +2.06, +1.88 |
| target 4 bp | 84/82, 59/58 | +2.53, +2.25 | +2.92, +2.64 | +2.83, +2.43 |
| target 8 bp, no stop | **90/87, 82/81** | **+3.86, +2.87** | +3.94, +3.69 | +3.29, +3.36 |

Target 8 bp with no stop gives the top UIDs' fingerprint (62–71 kept, nearly all positive, +3.1 to +3.9 bp median). Books ≥ 63: 50/47, 38/37 kept. The 1 h stop never binds within these 40-sim-min chunks, so stop vs no stop is untested here.
My parked-losers idea is only a small part: α exceeds raw P&L by ≤ 0.65 bp; the main gain is bigger moves per notional. Open positions charge one leg of notional, which flatters the wider targets. Paper runs 2–3× optimistic and has misled twice today.

**Proposal (awaiting the user):** re-arm x1's 18-minute-old test as A clock control, B 4 bp, C 8 bp, D 8 bp no stop.

## §1262 — Why top makers earn where x3 does not: x3 is adversely selected, slow and rarely reprices (2026-11-06, 9:18 PM CT)

m300.py on odd $300 books since sim min 1327 (x3 364 fills, top UIDs 144/252/7/31 398): fill vs mid +0.97 vs +1.58 bp; mid vs fill after 20 s +0.13 vs +1.72. Net of the distance from the mid, the move after the fill is **x3 −0.84 vs top +0.14 bp**. At the touch alone: −0.71 vs +0.30. (My first reading, "filled ahead of the move", overstated it; that metric includes the fill's own offset.) Per-book side balance in the window: x3 0.82, top 0.29, both sides on 61 of 117 UID-books. Taker mix: 92% background for top, 77% for x3.
Ruled out: fill size (all books: at $1–2k, top +5.89 vs x3 +1.47 after 20 s); v3 agreement sorts x3's fills in order (+0.5 / −0.1 / −0.6 / −3.2 bp at 60 s from strongly with to strongly against) but 96% of $ sits in the mild middle, so a filter moves the mean ≈ 0.1 bp.

**Public gauges, x3 vs 144 / 252 / 7 / 31:** call_time median 0.213 s vs 0.069–0.109; placements_sent 657 vs ≈ 5,000–6,000; cancels_sent 651 vs ≈ 3,100; at-best seconds 20,574 vs 37,000–46,000; best size 0.89M vs 1.4–1.7M; fills in the sample period 65 vs 30–55. **They respond 2–3× faster, reprice about 8× more often, and fill less per quote.** A stale quote is what gets picked off. x3 at the touch also spends its budget at once and then sits out, while quotes behind the touch keep them in the book without spending.

**Next:** measure where x3's 0.2 s goes (tape, qlog, per-book work) and cut it; then check why it reprices so rarely.

Handler profile on captured states (x3's params, 24 steps): `_Ev` build ≈ 22% + event/book wrappers ≈ 44% together, `_record` (tape) ≈ 20%, `_predict` ≈ 13%. Parse + decompress ≈ 30 ms. The live gauge reads 213 ms vs ≈ 95 ms of agent work, so ≈ 120 ms is outside this code (axon, network, reply).

Last sim hour: 1,304 fills, $1.58M, median fill $1,528; one such fill uses 293 sim s of a book's budget. Being at the touch, a quote fills fast, spends that, then the book waits. So the 8× repricing gap is partly pacing (≈ 3×), not all of it.

## §1270 — x3's one-sided books are trending books; front-loaded budget built (not deployed) (2026-11-07, 10:58 AM CT)

**One-sided books (onesided.py, x3, new sim, print-centred capture by side):** 25 of 65 books have one side ≤ 0. **Front-loaded budget (QuoteAgent `pace_start`, `pace_steady`; default off):** a book with no volume history starts with pace_start dollars; the bucket refills at pace_steady per 24 h and never refills above the normal burst, so the start is spent once. pace_cap stays the 24-h backstop. Tests (test_pace.py), pace_cap 450k / steady 350k / start 100k: worst 24 h $450,991 ($3k orders), $452,161 ($10k), $458,487 (one $50k sweep each time), all under $500k. A fresh book trades $102,000 before its first pause vs $6,000 normally. The first day's total is not cut ($450,991). The start is never refilled ($3,646 after a long wait). A restart does not re-grant it to a book with history. Replay identical with it off (865 / 1,002). **Trade-off:** after the first day the steady pace is 350k instead of 450k (−22%); a smaller start (e.g. steady 400k + start 50k) trades less of one for the other. Deploy only on a NEW UID, and only with the user's yes.

## §1332 — 2026-11-08 10:23 PM CT — 4-dec order pile-up bug found 3 min into test 2; fixed; test-2 window restarted
- INS OVER on book 122 (4-dec) at 10:22 PM: 7 cancels + 1 place in one reply. Cause: with the wide 4-dec keep tolerance (k/2 ≈ 135 ticks, span ≈ 1.5 k) every touch
  order left behind by a price move was KEPT as if it were a ladder order and a new touch order placed → orders piled up (real-cancel test: 10 per side after
  10 rising rounds on the live agent); when the spread then fell below 3 ticks the fallback base path cancelled them one by one (8 instructions > 5).
- Fix (QuoteAgent.py md5 dd1e5d40 = deployed; backups agents/QuoteAgent.pre-decfix.py / repo QuoteAgent.pre-decfix.py): with a tolerance given, _vol_ladder keeps
  only orders within tol of a level (others between the touch and the level are cancelled as stale); 4-dec books with a too-tight spread pull everything with
  ONE cancel_orders. test_pace: real-cancel pile-up test (fixed: max 2 per side; live agent FAILS with 10) + 7 stale orders → ≤ 5 instructions — ALL PASS.
- Registration gate passed; x3 restarted 10:23:31 PM CT (sim ≈ 30,570); test-2 read moved to 11:27 PM CT. Dropped gauge was 0 throughout.

## §1419 — 2026-11-12 7:45 PM CT — Deep dive: why our makers sit below the median (validator 0.6.7 + live gauges)
1. **The lab's validator copy is out of date:** upstream shipped 0.6.7 on 11-06 and 11-10 (the 256-book layout, class pools, the skill bar per class, takers charged against the mark). Read-only checkout: /opt/mvtrx/repo067 (git worktree). The running miners still import /opt/mvtrx/repo (0.6.6) — do not pull it under them.
2. **Each pay half is split by book class 50 / 25 / 25** (books 0–127 / 128–191 / 192–255), shares normalised inside each class. Class making totals now 112k / 35k / 5.4k, so one unit of credit is worth ≈ $0.13 / $0.20 / $1.34 a month. x1's 45 credit on the 4-dec books ≈ $60/mo, half its pay; its $300 books ≈ $14/mo.
3. **Half of all pay is the skill pool, and our makers get none of it:** eligible per class with kappa > 0 on ≥ 20 / 10 / 10 books whose alpha (MTM P&L − mean inventory × drift) clears 2.3 bp of the miner's own filled notional; paid ∝ net alpha (≈ $65–85/mo per +1,000). 160 of 256 miners qualify. x1: −154 / +5 / −234. UID 46: +683 / +968 / +4 → ≈ 56% of its pay is skill, while its making credit is BELOW x1's. Our high-volume first-level quoting earns ≈ 1 bp, under the 2.3 bp hurdle.
4. x2 is already skill-eligible on the $300 books (+298 on 42 books) despite its score 0.
Consequence: tests judged by edge per $ alone can pick the wrong winner (e.g. the deep-only 4-dec arm may raise edge but cut credit in the most valuable class). The 11-13 decision now weighs each arm by pay-weighted credit per class (making_exact per arm × $/credit per class) and by alpha vs the 2.3 bp hurdle.

## §1429 — 2026-11-13 ≈ 6:55 AM CT — Deep dive of the "test" branch link: nothing new there; the making collapse = the DYNAMIC MAKER FEE (missed until now)
- github taos-im/sn-79 branch "test" = main = 20e9785 "0.6.7 final" (11-10) — the version already live; open PRs are from August. Only paid-scoring default changed
  0.6.6 → 0.6.7: none (mark_mode_alt last → median is published, not paid). Missed until now: the engine's FeePolicy type="dynamic" and the making fee netting.
- Engine (simulate/trading/src/cpp/matching/DynamicFeePolicy.cpp, config simulation_*.xml): base maker 0, taker 2.3 bp; PER BOOK the passive share of MINER volume
  (agentId ≥ 0; background excluded) over the book's last 300 trade slots, MTR = passive ÷ (passive + aggressive); target 0.4; above it the maker FEE rises as
  coef × (MTR − 0.4)^2 toward maxMakerRate 1.5% (150 bp) and takers get the same as a REBATE. → too much miner making vs miner taking on a book = high maker fees.
- Measured (tape, Mf / notional): current run $300 82 → 109 → 114 bp, $30 119 → 128 bp, 4-dec 38 → 90 → 44 bp (rising through the run); previous runs' $300 mostly
  20–40 bp (−3…+76). Per book now 100–141 bp; differences between makers on a book = timing.
- Validator: making credit per maker fill = (mid − price)·q − making_fee_weight × Mf, weight 0.005 (help: "stepped… raised at later boundaries") → at 110–140 bp the
  netting is 0.55–0.7 bp per fill vs our $300 edge ≈ 1.2–1.3 bp before the 20-s markout → realized ≤ 0 for thin-edge makers → the field-wide making decay (§1428).
  Fees are NOT in skill (debeta mtm: only the taker's fill-vs-mark charge) → taker rebates pay nothing in scoring; skill unaffected (fleet still paid).
- What still earns $300 making now: wider/deeper quotes — UID 23 (top $300 maker) 79% of $ ≥ 2 ticks back, edge at fill +2.3 bp vs ours +1.3.
- Levers: (1) live now: mk_vol_touch_min N (no $300 touch order while the spread < N ticks) + a deeper $300 ladder → more edge per fill; (2) next build: read
  accounts[book].fees maker_fee_rate each round and require half-spread ≥ 0.005 × rate + margin per book (skip/widen high-fee books); (3) the fee is a field-wide
  per-book state driven by miner maker/taker mix — skill-first remains the robust path.

## §1459 — 2026-11-14 2:15 PM CT — Speed build 9f0d07f3 (from 10dc929d): agent 200 → 67 ms median, output IDENTICAL; not deployed (no miner)
Measured on 5 fresh validator requests captured off the wire (tcpdump on :8102 + reassembly → /opt/mvtrx/cap14/req_*.json, 256 books, ≈ 1.7 MB, ≈ 22–27k events,
29k resting orders per state; bench /opt/mvtrx/speed/bench.py with the live x2 unit params + live_params_174.json). Live cycle before (journal): decompress ≈ 0.10 s,
update 0.07–0.16, respond 0.22–0.27, instruction printing 0.01–0.03; gauge call_time_median 174 = 0.531 s vs 252 0.128 / 216 0.129.
Fixes (all exact — no strategy change):
1. _RawBook.events built lazily (raw dicts kept in raw_e) — the _Ev build of every event was the biggest cost.
2. Pace fill scan reads the raw dicts; builds an _Ev only for our own fills.
3. Tape (_record) written by ONE FIFO background thread, 0.25 s after the state and only once the handler is idle (tape_async=1, tape_delay=0.25).
4. Per-book instruction count (_vol_ladder / _vol_lazy) counts from this book's start index — was a scan of the whole reply for every book (quadratic).
5. Lock folder listed once per state (set) instead of ≈ 1,500 stat calls; our own ack writes/removes keep the set in sync.
6. quiet_report=1: one "REPLIES" line per sim minute instead of printing ≈ 600 instructions per state before replying (also stops the journal bloat behind the scan hangs).
Results: agent handle median 200 → 67 ms (p90 310 → 76) with the tape off the reply path; side by side vs 10dc929d on the same states (equiv.py, lock folder seeded from

## §1484 — 2026-11-15 2:45 PM CT — The subnet's goal and the market's actual model (README, FAQ, simulate/trading/run/config/simulation_0.xml) → strategy implications
GOAL (README/FAQ): realistic, valuable market DATA from "intelligent, risk-averse, budget-constrained" agents. Making pays two-sided liquidity that is not run over (20-s markout);
skill pays "profit the market's drift does not explain" (inventory × mid change, drift removed; consistent across books, ≥ 20/10/10 books; qualifying miners share the half by
net alpha); "pay follows performance, not volume"; "a strategy confined to a few books earns little"; fees + spread paid are in skill P&L (takers); weekly config changes;
response time → order delay.
MARKET MODEL ($300 books, simulation_0.xml; 8 × 16 books): fundamental = fBM Hurst 0.729 (persistent), σ 0.0069, jumps λ 2.06e-4 σJ 0.00622, updated every 30 s, published to us;
1,000 StylizedTraderAgents (Chiarella 2007): sigmaF 1.2 (fundamentalist), sigmaC 1.1 (chartist), sigmaN 0.7 (noise), tau 600 s, tauHist 50 s; 20 HFT market makers (spread 15 bp,
minSpreadTicks 10, undercutTicks 5, inventory horizon); 1,024 noise traders; 1 ALGO trader per book (large meta-orders, updateInterval 60 s, immediateBase 600); FeePolicy dynamic
(targetMTR 0.4, maker 0 / taker 2.3 bp base, max 1.5%); minOrderSize 0.25; maxOpenOrders 100; MagneticField + FuturesSignal processes (FuturesTraderAgent count 0).
MEASURED (speed/takerid.py, last ≈ 1,430 sim s, $300): taker id −1 = the big-sweep taker — median $5,802 per taker-second, 93% of its $ in $10k+ events, 60-s mid move its way
−0.04 bp → UNINFORMED, impact reverts; miner takers +0.44 bp (informed); other bg ids ≈ $600 events, ±0.2 bp.
IMPLICATIONS: (1) skill counts only inventory × mid move (maker fill price not credited) → fills that happen while a sweep pushes price through our orders are structurally bad
for skill; fleet fills = small flow at/inside the touch; supports the redo (one order per side, gated step-ins). (2) The price model is known → build the lean from it
(fundamental gap + fundamental trend (Hurst 0.73) + ≈ 50-s chartist momentum − sweep reversion), held-out tested vs fade / fund-move leans. (3) Sweeps revert in ≈ 60 s →
consider holding sweep-acquired inventory ≈ 60 s instead of unwinding. (4) DIS fees reward scarce liquidity — fee-aware already reads per-book maker fees.
NEXT: offline fit of the model-based predictor (MEASURED, held-out) during the fade test; if it beats the fade it becomes the redo's step-in side; sweep-hold queued.

## §1500 — 2026-11-15 9:10 PM CT — What killed our makers (≈ $190/mo on 11-09) and whether it can recur with the new edge (user Q)
Killers (§1289, §1364, §1429, §1438–§1447): (1) our income was the MAKING half; the engine's DYNAMIC maker fee (per book, rises when miner making share > 0.4) went from 20–40 bp to
100–140 bp; the validator nets 0.005 × fee from making credit → making ≈ 0 field-wide by 11-13 (even 252); making quality is one miner-wide factor → one bad class zeroed all;
(2) 0.6.7 (11-10): 256 books / 3 classes — our tuning was for 128; (3) ours: three identical makers on the same books (11-08) split flow and skill (x3 $158 → $56 overnight), tests /
restarts on settled miners, start bursts burning the pace budget before protection ended.
Recurrence risk for the REDO: it earns SKILL (inventory × mid move, drift removed; fees not in it) — the fee mechanism that killed making doesn't apply. Real risks: (a) weekly releases
can change market configs / skill rules → after every release re-read the configs and REFIT the model before trusting it; (b) crowding (skill qualifiers 172–189 → 213–219 on 11-15)
dilutes share; (c) scaling identical miners on the same books collides (as 11-08) → split books / vary thresholds and run the collision checks before adding miners; (d) unproven over
hours / the validator window / protection end (≈ 3:10 PM 11-16). Plan adds: post-release refit + compare; collision plan before scaling; auto-revert for tweaks once a winner (user).

debeta.kappa_of_alpha: MAD-normalised, downside-adjusted mean of per-book alphas (books with |alpha| ≥ the floor, ≥ min books) — "magnitude-blind". reward.skill_pool_share: eligible if skill_raw > 0 on ≥ min_books
qualifying books; share = max(0, skill_net_alpha) × p11 counterparty factor ÷ total ("consistency decides who is in, P&L decides how much"; cloning-invariant). → 252's kappa 3–4 = very even per-book results
(big steady fleet); its pay ($212) comes from net alpha ≈ 1,700. Ours: gate passed (0.97 / 0.94); what to grow is net alpha. Net alpha is a rolling-window total (window = several sim h ≈ a wall day at
today's sim speed) → still filling for 85/47; last 15 sim min 85 +93.8, 47 +147.6 vs 252 +46.5 → at full window each could pass 252's ≈ 1,700 if the per-minute edge holds (crowding / sim reset / release risks).

## §1565 — 2026-11-17 1:45 AM CT — SYNTH (SN50) $-model check (user: "lets run the synth test"): the forward test's $4.4–5.8k/UID is NOT credible; realistic ≈ $150–600/UID, slow ramp
Chain (deploy/sn50/sn50pay.py, TAO $193): miner $ ≈ $60.6k/mo of $121k; UID 248 (639 d, ck 5DxyiWpG) $13.3k = 22% of miner $ (owner-like; 0% in the 24h API view); best real miners: 215 $1,106 (51 d),
then ≈ 14 UIDs at $539–870 (fleet 5Cu4VX5C at a flat $539); paid median $115, p90 $539. Synth API v2/leaderboard/latest (fractions of total): default/1h view top 163 1.025%, then ≈ 1.0% flat;
prompt_name=high (24h) top 216 0.656%, 66 0.319%, 251 0.318% — i.e. the real 24h competition is FLAT-ish, not winner-take-most.
Validator code (synth-subnet 10-28): 3 competitions (com/equ 24h, crypto 24h, crypto 1h; + VHFT) ≈ ¼ each; softmax β 0.15 (24h) / 0.3 (1h) over a MOVING AVERAGE (window 10 d for 24h, 5 d for 1h) of
per-asset-weighted scores (ASSET_COEFFICIENTS: BTC 1.0, ETH 0.71, SOL 0.63, XRP 0.57, HYPE 0.48, …); miners that joined inside the window get the WORST score backfilled for the missing times.
Sanity check of our backtest's share method (deploy/sn50/synthcheck.py, 10 forward days, 1,232 prompt-asset rows): the same method predicts the field's best 24h UID (163) takes 39–89% of the competition —
REAL: 163 gets 0.0% there (it is 5.0 d old: a re-used slot, so the historical API's per-UID scores include the PREVIOUS owner, and the validator backfills the new owner's missing days with the worst score).
The real 24h leaders 216 / 66 / 251 are 10.2–11.2 d old (just past the 10-day window). → The backtest (field scores keyed by UID, no backfill, no asset coefficients) does not reproduce the validator; its
"rank 1, 32% share, ≈ $5.7k/mo" is an artefact. With coefficients our model's average is still slightly better than the field's best in our reconstruction (49.8 vs 54.7) but that comparison is not trusted.
Realistic: crypto-1h ≈ 2× median (≈ $150/mo, §1222) + whatever 24h share survives; pay ≈ 0 for the first ≈ 5 d (1h) / 10 d (24h) because of the worst-score backfill; SN50 immunity 65,535 blocks ≈ 9.1 d.
Verdict: Synth is a small, slow stream (≈ $150–600/UID after ≈ 10 days), well below MVTRX per UID; keep staged, do NOT register on the backtest's $; a credible estimate needs the validator's own
moving-average path (prepare_df_for_moving_average + coefficients) re-run on the history with per-hotkey (not per-UID) keys.

fill's own print and the W = 15 nearest PRINTS on each side (trade prices, dust-floored, reach 8W) — NOT the book mid; realized R = the same against the print mark 20 s of sim time later; both net of
fee_weight 0.005 × the maker fee (dynamic MTR fee ≈ 138–143 bp now → ≈ 0.7 bp per fill); self-trades earn nothing. Per book two-sided = 2·min(buy C, sell C); quality = clamp(ΣR/ΣC over ALL of the miner's
books, 0, 1) (taker legs booked apart); credit per class = Σ two-sided × quality; making pool split by class 50 / 25 / 25 ($300 / $30 / 4-dec), share of class credit.
→ stepping INSIDE the spread to buy pays above the surrounding prints → negative C (why 85's C is −25.9 / R −37.9); exactly-at-the-touch balanced fills capture the half-spread (+1.8 bp) − 0.7 fee.

## §1596 — 2026-11-17 3:50 PM CT — Why 85/47 stopped at ≈ 1,100–1,200 net alpha (user question) — correction of my 11-16 projection
Net alpha is a ROLLING sum over the validator's ≈ 200-sim-min window (checked §1586: our 200-min sums match the gauges), so it levels off at ≈ alpha per sim min × 200 once a miner is older than the window.
85/47 earn ≈ 5–5.5 per sim min ($300 ≈ 3.5–4 + $30 ≈ 1–1.5) → ≈ 1,100–1,200. My 11-16 estimate of a ≈ 5.5-sim-h window (from a rough 252 comparison) made me project continued growth through 11-17 — wrong:
the windows were full by the morning. Lesson: verify the window length directly before projecting.
Per-minute gap to 5E2fVqiW (≈ 9 per sim min → ≈ 2,000): we don't quote when there is no lean (14% of our $ vs their 38–44% at +1.0…+1.8 bp), our $1–3.6k step-ins fill partially and wait for the
budget (447 vs 770 fills), their small lean-side fills earn more per $ (+2.4…+2.7 vs +1.5), and two of our copies cost each other 15–20%. Targets: ≈ 6.5+ per sim min to clear ≈ $105–110; ≈ 9–10 for $150–200.

## §1603 — 2026-11-17 4:43 PM CT — H3 taker test live on UID 228 (user: "start the test on 228")

**Why H2 churned (§1601), from the code:**
- No limit on open books: each of the 128 $300 books built its own $4k position, $600 at a time.
- No miner-wide trade-rate limit: 15-s add gap and 5-s retries meant about 2 IOCs per book per sim min.
- A lock was released only when a book's position reached its target. Paced and unfunded paths left locks behind, which kept 85/47/54 quotes pulled.

**Agent 570517c8 (from e2ce0136)** adds new knobs, all off by default:
- `mk_take_books`: max open-target books.
- `mk_take_rate`: miner-wide entry IOCs per sim min (token bucket).
- `mk_take_k`: entries only when |pred| ≥ k × thr.
- `mk_take_hold`: close after that many seconds with no add.

Locks now span one IOC: they are released after each IOC and on every paced, unfunded or empty-bucket return. If the rest of an order can't be funded, the miner keeps the units it has.

Verification:
- equiv.py: 0 instruction diffs; tape, ledger and locks identical.
- test_pace ALL PASS.
- newminer.sh now expects 570517c8 (backup newminer.sh.bak-h3).

## §1605 — 2026-11-17 5:40 PM CT — why the tests fail (alpha study) + REST-NONE test live on 54 (user: "run the offline test and the live one on 54"; tests pre-approved)

**Alpha study** (speed/alphadecomp(2).py, twosided3.py, nahist.py; window 81300–83080 before the tests):
- **Pay = net alpha** (de-drifted inventory MTM over every filled book) × p11, for eligible miners. Spread capture doesn't count. Making credit is 0 for 47, 54, 85 and 252 (validator gauges), so the making half pays us nothing.
- **Validator net alpha:** 85 ≈ 1,050–1,200, 47 ≈ 1,130–1,270, 252 ≈ 1,600–1,770.
- **Every miner is pace-bound** at ≈ $38k per sim min of $300 volume (the 24-h sim-time cap). Share of book-rounds resting on the GATE: 85 99% (after the fleet test burned its bucket), 54 51%, 47 11%.
- So the lever is alpha per dollar of budget. Fill move after 120 s:

  | Miner | 120-s move | Volume | Where the volume goes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 252 | +1.63 bp | $1.13M | big fills ($2–3.5k); even its weak-signal fills earn +1.3 bp |
  | 47 | +1.54 bp | $0.64M | 89% on lean |
  | 85 | +0.88 bp | — | 36% in small ~$300 no-lean / against fills at the touch (the gate's rest orders), −0.4 to −1.9 bp |
  | 54 | +0.88 bp | — | 42% of $ at P < 1 thr: 36% at P 0.5–1 (+0.19 bp), many 30 ticks back |

- **Why the tests fail:** 85's fleet copy added no-lean quoting, which earns ≈ 0 for us, and burned its budget. 47's hold-longer is the most budget-efficient miner, but its read fell in a slow market.
- 54's inventory is flat (< $1k) 33% of the time, 85's and 47's ≈ 50%, 252's 33%.

**Test: `mk_rest_none 1` on 54** (agent e29ace21 = 570517c8 + the knob):
- No gated $300 rest orders at all: non-lean sides, no-lean books and low-bucket rests are all removed. The budget goes only to lean step-ins.
- The same agent also fixes the H3 unfunded path, which now restarts the hold clock.
- Verification: equiv 0 diffs; tape, ledger and locks identical; test_pace ALL PASS. Census (speed/rncensus.py): arm A rests $360 orders 32 ticks back on vol/calm; arm B places none.
- **Interaction check:**
  - Unchanged: lean jump/step-in, part step-in, $30 books (not gated), fee push, no-chase, lock acks.
  - Coverage of $300 books will drop. Coverage only scales skill_raw, while pay needs skill_raw > 0 and skill_books ≥ the bar. The watch_extra coverage alert for 54 was lowered to 120 (backup .bak-rn).
  - Inventory now shrinks only through opposite-lean step-ins (longer holds); max_inv still caps it.
- Restart 23:40:09 UTC (sim ≈ 84070). Warm-up until ≈ 84370. Backup live_params_54.pre-restnone.json. newminer.sh now expects e29ace21.
- **Baseline** (last 45 sim min, 81361–84061):

  | 47 | +163.1 | +85.6 | 5.5 |
  | 252 | +99.5 | +44.9 | — |

  54's $300 ratio to 47 is 1.25×.

## §1630 — 2026-11-18 12:40 AM CT — scaling ceiling study (user: "each lane can only house 2–3 miners … can't create enough lanes at 200/m?")

- **Pool size** (speed/poolsize.py, chain emission × price): total miner pay ≈ $56,750/mo over 248 paid UIDs.
  - Median $185; p75 $279; 111 UIDs > $200; top $1,050.
  - Split ≈ $28k making / $28k skill. Skill by class 50/25/25 → $300 ≈ $14.2k, $30 ≈ $7.1k, 4-dec ≈ $7.1k.
  - We earn only skill on $300 + $30 → our addressable pool ≈ $21.3k/mo (making share = 0 for all of ours).
- **Fleet evidence** (fleets.json × gauges × pay):

  | Fleet | UIDs | Earns from | Median net α | Total pay | Per UID |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | **5E2fVqiW** | 20 | skill only, making 0 — same kind as ours | 1,627 | $3,290/mo | $154–174, median $165 |
  | 5CAXJT4t | 35 | — | — | $5,794 | median $178 |
  | 5GCSdbyd | 17 | — | — | $4,328 | median $265 |
  | 5F1F2JMu | 27 | 26 making + 16 skill | — | $5,396 | median $153 |

  - 5E2fVqiW: 20 near-identical $300 makers on the same books; the copies do NOT deplete each other's alpha to nothing.
- **Conclusions:**
  1. Lanes are not the only way to scale: 20 identical skill makers each hold ≈ 1,600 net α (≈ $165). Per-miner alpha is limited mostly by each UID's own volume cap, and the uninformed flow is large next to one UID's cap.
     Our own copy cost (−15–20% for 2, §1568; re-measured tonight) is the number to watch: if the loss stops growing with more copies (as the fleet shows), copies scale.
  2. **Dilution:** pay is a share of a fixed pool. If 54 reaches ≈ 2,000 net α (≈ $0.10/unit today), 20 copies add ≈ 40k units to the ≈ 210k-unit $300+$30 pool → ≈ −16% per unit (≈ $170 each). 40 copies → ≈ −27% (≈ $145 each).
     So 20 × $200 ($4k ≈ 19% of the pool) is hard but in the range the top fleets reach ($3.3k–5.8k); 40 × $200 ($8k ≈ 38% of our pool) is not realistic from skill alone.
  3. $10k+/mo needs more than one pool: the making half ($28k, where 5F1F2JMu, 5ECLVeLz, 5GVu1hrR and 5FNTAiDo earn) and/or 4-dec ($7k), on separate miners. Skill-only copies plausibly cap around $3–4k/mo for us.
- **Next research:** after tonight's copy test, project copies-vs-lanes with dilution; study what makes 5E2fVqiW's no-lean fills profitable (dF10 counterparty effect, §1628); revisit a making-credit miner design for the $28k half.

## §1631 — 2026-11-18 12:55 AM CT — do copies divide alpha? 5E2fVqiW history + our own 2-copy data (user Q)

- **Hypothesis (user):** maybe one miner would earn ≈ 20× what each of the fleet's 20 copies earns (alpha simply divided).
- **speed/fleethist.py, 5E2fVqiW, 10 days at 6-h steps** (validator net alpha of its current UIDs):
  - If alpha were divided, the fleet TOTAL would stay roughly constant and the per-UID median would fall as more copies trade.
  - Observed: the total moves with the number of active copies, 1.8k (6 UIDs, 11-11) → 41k (20 UIDs, 11-17). The median is HIGHEST with all 20 active (1,600–2,055 on 11-17).
    With 6–9 active it was 209–819. So more copies coincided with more total and NOT lower per-copy alpha.
  - Caveat: the active count isn't controlled (bad market regimes also turn copies negative), so this is correlation, not proof.
- **Our direct test (controlled):** 85 alone → 85 + 47 identical gave ≈ 1.7× one miner's alpha (§1568: −15–20% per miner), not 1× as a pure division would.
- **Mechanism:** each UID has its own per-book volume cap, so 20 copies have 20× the budget. Fills come from a large uninformed flow, so copies mostly add fills rather than split a fixed set.
  The cost is partial overlap (we measure it tonight), not a 1/N split.
- **Proof plan:** tonight's copy test (2 copies on the new recipe), then measure the incremental α of each added copy when we scale (copy 3, 4, …); stop adding when the increment gets small.

  The 47 test (§1600) had no ceiling, so it never hit this.

- **Lesson:** for any lean-gating knob, check it against the band (exit_k × model_lean must be < model_lean_max).

## §1661 — 2026-11-18 12:00 PM CT — $30 offline study, part 1: where 54's $30 alpha leaks

- **speed/twosided3b.py** (MODEL=model_lean_30, BOOKS=128–191; old day 78000–86400; header says "$300" but these are $30 books):

  | Model signal at the fill (P = |pred| / thr_30, signed) | 54 share of $ | 54 size | 54 120-s move | 252 share of $ |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Against (≤ −1) | 7% | $600 | −2.17 bp | 8% |
  | −1..0 | 24% | $600 | −0.42 bp | 45% |
  | 0..0.5 | 15% | $600 | +0.23 bp | 21% |
  | 0.5..1 | 26% | $1.6k | +0.63 bp | — |
  | 1..1.5 | 21% | $1.6k | +1.07 bp | — |
  | ≥ 1.5 | 7% | $1.6k | +1.88 bp | — |

  - Almost all at the touch. **252 is no better per fill** (P < 0.5 = 74% of its $, its P ≥ 1 fills +1.7–1.8 bp, all at $1.8k).
    So 252's occasional $30 lead (§1637/§1650) is not better fill selection; probably longer holds or bigger positions. Today's 33-min window had 54 +1.23 vs 252 +1.00 bp on $30.
- **Source of the no-lean $30 orders:** mk_lean30_only=1 (§1495) by design keeps BOTH sides MK_LEAN30_BACK (2) ticks back when there is no $30 lean. The census (speed/low2census.py) shows full-size $1.65k orders 3 ticks behind on no-lean books.
  The $30 ladder is NOT the source (mk_low_lad_size 0 leaves them unchanged).
- **Fix options:**
  1. A "$30 rest_none" knob (no $30 orders without a lean, nothing on the non-predicted side). This needs agent code, so a RESTART — not allowed while the user is away. Ask first.
  2. Live: mk_lean30_back 2 → deeper. Likely worse: deep fills come from sweeps through the level, the same adverse selection rest-30 showed on $300 (−1 bp).
- **Size of the prize:** dropping the P < ≈0.75 no-lean fills (≈ 46% of $30 $, net ≈ −0.3 bp) → $30 α ≈ +15–20%, plus freed pace budget → ≈ +0.2–0.4 α per sim min per miner (≈ +$5–10/mo).

- **speed/runover.py** (live_tape_x5.jsonl, 14050–now): $300 maker fills by run-over = mid move into the order over the last 10 s, with the 120-s after-fill move vs the fill price.

  | Run-over (bp into the order) | < 0 | 0–0.5 | 0.5–1 | 1–2 | 2–4 | > 4 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Fleet 1 / 29 / 62 share of $ | 27–32% | 26–30% | 13–15% | 13–17% | 9–12% | 2–3% |
  | Fleet after-fill move | +2.5–2.9 bp in every bin | | | | | |
  | 228 share of $ | 8% | 15% | 16% | 28% | 27% | 5% |
  | 228 after-fill move | +2.0–2.8 bp in every bin | | | | | |
  | 38 share of $ | 20% | 26% | 19% | 22% | 11% | 1% |
  | 38 after-fill move | +1.2–1.7 bp (+3.0 at > 4) | | | | | |

- **Reading:**
  - Run-over fills pay about as well as fresh ones for everyone, so an anti-run-over rule would not help (idea from §1700 dropped).
  - The real difference: 228's fills are concentrated in run-over situations (60% at ≥ 1 bp). Our model leans on reversion after moves (negative weights on r50/r300), so we only fill when price has just moved.
  - The fleet fills mostly when nothing has moved (57–60% at ≤ 0.5 bp) and still gains +2.2–2.6 bp. They have a predictor that works at ALL times, which explains copy-robustness: they don't depend on the few post-move moments we all compete for.

## §1711 — 2026-11-19 6:00 AM CT — WHY PAY LAGS: a track-record EMA with half-life = 3 SIM hours (≈ 18 wall h at today's speed); survival bar ≈ steady ≥ 1.7× the prune line

- **Brief:** pay 228 $86, 38 $14, 252 $191. Validator net α: 228 1,570, 252 1,359, 38 1,078. Prune line $103. Both REGISTERED, 0 errors.

  | Emission | 0.238 | 0.532 | 0.039 |
  | Incentive | 0.0016 | 0.0036 | 0.0003 |
  | Net α | 1,570 | 1,359 | 1,078 |

  - skill_p11_factor ≈ 1, coverage 1, pool factor 1, weight 1 for all three. Pay ≠ proportional to current net α.
- **Validator config:** `scoring.score_ema_halflife` = scoring.kappa.lookback = 3 h of SIM time. "Per-UID track-record EMA applied to the trading score before allocation … a strong window converts into standing only gradually."
  - At ≈ 10 sim s per wall min: ≈ 18 wall h half-life. A new UID's pay ≈ 1 − 2^(−t/18 h) of steady: ≈ 42% at 14 h (228 now: steady ≈ $150–170 → ≈ $86–90 ✓), ≈ 60% at 24 h (immunity end), ≈ 75% at 36 h.
- **Consequences:**
  - Every prune so far (85, 47, 54, old 228) happened while pay showed ≈ ½ of steady.
  - Survival at immunity end needs a steady value ≥ prune line / 0.6 ≈ 1.7× the line (≈ $175 today).
  - x3 (steady ≈ $150–170) is BORDERLINE: expect pay ≈ $90–100 at 3:25 PM vs a line ≈ $103, so a prune is possible shortly after.
  - Faster sim days shorten the wall-clock catch-up (the half-life is sim time).
- **Under the long-run rule x3 stays untouched.** Lesson: projected steady pay must clear ≈ 1.7× the prune line for a miner to survive its first immunity end. This supersedes the 1.3× survival gate (§1598) for new registrations; tell the user.

- Per dollar, our fills behind the touch earn about the same long-horizon value as our inside step-ins (2.5 vs 2.75 bp on 228; 2.1 vs 2.1 on 38), and do better at 20 s.
- The fleet's behind fills earn more than both.
- So moving volume from inside to behind need not cost skill **if volume is kept** (we are pace-bound either way). The risk is fill volume, not edge per $.
- **Value check** (incentive → $ ≈ $53k per unit):
  - Skill-only 5E2fVqiW: ≈ $0.07/month per net α.
  - UID 55: 0.0047 incentive (≈ $250/mo) = ≈ $70 skill (α 999) + ≈ $180 making (share 0.0065).
  - Losing even 40% of 228's α (≈ −$50/mo) is outweighed by a making share near the fleet's (≈ +$180/mo).
- M3 design: keep the lean signal; post the lean-side order AT or BEHIND the touch in larger size instead of stepping inside.
  - Before starting: census for interactions with every live knob.
  - Read on skill α per $ AND validator quality.

## §1738 — 5:30–5:37 PM CT — start burst explained + fixed (pace_cold); 113 moved to x3's (228) lean lane

- **Why the start burst hurts making:**
  - Each book's token bucket starts at max(rate × pace_burst, pace_start) = $5.21/sim s × 3,600 = **$18.75k per book** (192 books ≈ $3.6M), against a steady refill of ≈ $312 per book per sim min. Every start AND every restart front-loads ≈ 60 sim min of trading into the first minutes.
  - Those fills come from brand-new orders at the back of every queue, so they fill mostly when sweeps eat whole levels. That gave 113 $30 R −10 on $1.04M in 8 sim min.
  - The fills stay in the validator's making window (≈ 180 sim min ≈ 15 wall h at ≈ 11.7 sim s per wall min), dragging miner-wide quality for most of the first day.
  - It also inflates early skill α, which later leaves the window (the 54 lesson).
- **Fix:**
  - Agent **d8d9f7a7** = 2457bbcf + unit param `pace_cold` (1 = a new bucket starts at min(pace_start, burst) instead of a full burst; the refill and the 3,600-s burst cap are unchanged).
  - equiv 0 diffs (tape, ledger, locks identical); test_pace ALL PASS with it off.
  - With it on, 4 start-up assumption tests "fail" by design: no full burst at start, first-day total $355k vs $450k, two soft-pacing tests that assume a full bucket. Every hard-cap test passes.
  - mvtrx-x3.service: pace_start 4700 → **1500 + pace_cold=1** (backup /opt/mvtrx/mvtrx-x3.service.bak-cold). newminer.sh expects d8d9f7a7.
- **Lean:** 113 was on 38's band lane (lean 1.0, max 1.5). It is now on x3 228's lane: **mk_model_lean 1.5, no ceiling** (228 reached net α 1,841 with the best $300 α per $: +1.8–2.2 bp vs 38's +0.9–1.5). Backup live_params_113.pre-lean15.json. That lane is free since 228's prune. Revisit lanes when scaling.
- Restart 5:37 PM (sim s 28,743). 113 now = M2 + M3a + M3b2 + M4 (jump_back 1) + lean 1.5 + cold start.
- The M4 read at 6:47 PM covers this combination against the fleet refs (there is no same-time control).

## §1739 — 5:43–5:45 PM CT — CORRECTION to §1738: restarts do NOT re-burst; pace_cold on a running miner blocked it → reverted

- Check at 5:43 PM: after the cold restart, **153–155 of 190 books blocked** and 0 fills. No PACE SYNC charges.
- Cause: at start the agent replays the whole pace ledger through the buckets (lines 199–203), so a restart RESUMES the previous balance.
  - With pace_cold 1, the replay assumed 113's first bucket (4:11 PM) began at $1,500 instead of $18,750, then subtracted the real start-burst fills (≈ $19k per book). Most books ended below the −$5,000 soft floor, i.e. blocked for hours (refill ≈ $312 per sim min).
- **Corrections to §1738:**
  - (1) Restarts never re-burst; only a brand-new UID with an empty ledger does. 113's 5:28 restart did not add a burst.
  - (2) pace_cold must be set before a miner's FIRST start and never changed for that miner's life, because the replay must match how it really started.
- Fix 5:45 PM: mvtrx-x3.service back to pace_start=4700 pace_cold=0; restart → **0 of 190 books blocked**. The live knobs stay: lean 1.5 no ceiling + M2 + M3a + M3b2 + M4.
- For the NEXT new miner: set pace_cold=1 (+ pace_start ≈ 1,500) in its unit BEFORE its first start (newminer.sh does not do this yet).

## §1766 — 2:45 AM CT — offline: why 113's $300 validator R ≈ 0 while the fleet's is +17 to +24 (no live change)

## §1769 — 3:38 AM CT stage-3 watch: realized 4.79 but share still 0 → the pool is per CLASS

- **Live:**
  - 113: captured 66.2, realized 4.79, share 0.0000; net α **1,381**; incentive 0.0014; pay **$72/mo**.
  - 252: captured 162, realized 94, share 0.0048, net α 2,080.
- Why share stays 0 although realized > 0 (reward.py making_pool_inputs / class_pool_shares):
  - Share = max(0, making_raw) / Σ, normalised **within each class** ($300 / $30 / 4-dec), then mixed across classes at the class weights.
  - making_raw is two-sided per book: Σ_b 2·min(buy, sell) for that class, × miner-wide quality.
  - The captured/realized gauges are the uid's totals. A class whose two-sided sum is ≤ 0 contributes 0 share.
  - 113's $300 Σ2·min is −7 to −11 every window (lean side only) → $300 making share 0. The $30 class is positive in recent replicas (+5 to +12.5).
  - The published debeta_making_share is ≈ 0 so far. Most likely the $300 class dominates (largest weight), or the $30 two-sided total over the full window is not yet positive.
- ⇒ **M5 ($300 two-sided: rest the non-lean side behind the touch) is the step that unlocks the $300 making pool.** Planned for the morning (census + interaction check first; §1766).

## §1803 — 3:19 PM CT — user: keep fixing $300 making on this miner ("a maker-only miner failed for weeks"); per-fill validator-basis study finds the mechanism

speed/fillvalue.py: the validator's own accumulate_book_capture with _attribute_capture wrapped to record every maker fill's captured C and realized R; $300 books, last 30 sim min.

| uid | C per $ | R per $ | **R/C** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 113 | +0.28 bp | +0.01 bp | **0.04** |
| 55 | +0.28 bp | +0.10 bp | 0.37 |
| 252 | +0.31 bp | +0.16 bp | 0.52 |
| 210 | +0.35 bp | +0.20 bp | 0.56 |

- **Captured per $ is the same for all** (≈ 0.3 bp). The gap is entirely realized/captured.
- **113's losses:**
  - Single-level small hits: 1,108 fills, R/C −0.17 (fleet +0.39 to +0.61).
  - Fills 1 tick inside a sweep ("depth1"): $279k, R −2.07, R/C **−0.92** (fleet +0.17 to +0.31).
  - Deeper sweep fills (depth 2–3) are fine for everyone.
- **Interpretation:** our lean predicts minutes-scale moves. We buy into short-term dips (and sell into pops) that keep going for the next seconds. At the validator's 20-s horizon those fills look adverse; at 120–600 s they pay (our skill). The fleet barely leans on $300, so its fills are not tilted against the short-term move.
- **Skill α and 20-s making value conflict structurally on the lean side.** That is also why adding two-sided rests never fixed it, and why the maker-only miner failed.
- **Next tests (ABAB, judged on per-fill R/C via fillvalue.py + Σα vs 252):**
  1. **Delayed lean entry:** step in only once the last few seconds of prints stop moving against the lean (short-term momentum filter on the lean step-in).
  2. **Split books:** lean only where our 20-s R/C is positive; neutral (no lean, two-sided) elsewhere.

## §1807 — 3:53 PM CT — user: "can you get any information out of the test when it's pruned?" → offline counterfactual for delayed entry (speed/momcf.py)

- After a prune the tape stops (no more states). Blocks completed before it are still scored offline from the tape.
- More useful: tag every recorded fill by the mid move over the 10 sim s before it (vs the fill side), then score each group on the validator basis plus +120/+600 s quote-mid markouts (skill proxy).
- Last 90 sim min:

| uid / group | share of $300 $ | C per $ | R/C | +120 s | +600 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 113 against > 1 bp | 49% | +0.21 bp | **−0.41** | +2.17 bp | +1.93 bp |
| 113 against 0–1 bp | 28% | +0.17 bp | **−0.49** | +2.57 bp | +2.43 bp |
| 113 with / flat | 22% | **+0.42 bp** | **+0.18** | +2.03 bp | +2.02 bp |
| 113 all | — | +0.25 bp | −0.20 | +2.25 bp | +2.09 bp |
| 252 all (against > 1 bp: only 15%) | — | +0.32 bp | +0.57 | +2.66 bp | +3.00 bp |

- 252's R/C is ≈ 0.57 in every group.
- **Conclusions:**
  1. The §1803 diagnosis is confirmed: 77% of 113's $300 $ fills into an adverse 10-s move.
  2. Delayed entry should lift R/C (with/flat fills +0.18, C ×2) at **no per-$ skill cost** (+120/+600 s equal across groups). We are pace-bound, so the skipped budget is spent at better moments.
  3. The 0–1 bp group is as bad as > 1 bp → the stronger setting **mk_lean_mom_bp 0.0** should beat the live test's 1.0. Next variant.
  4. Even good fills reach only 0.18 vs 252's 0.57: delayed entry is a step, not the whole gap.
- This offline method lets the next miner start with the best setting without waiting for a live ABAB.

## §1833 — 11:00 PM CT — deep dive (user): what the subnet designs making credit to reward → a design-consistent making layer

**Design statements** (0.6.8 test-branch FAQ + config help):
- FAQ Q2: making = spread captured against the centred mid, two-sided per book, scaled by markout quality at 20 s.
- FAQ Q20: "quoting width, and how long a quote is left in front of flow, are what is priced. Resting time on its own is not paid."
- making_horizon_s help: **"past about 20 seconds the mark mostly measures the trend, which the skill half already prices with the drift removed."**
- Fees: DIS rewards liquidity where scarce. making_fee_weight is 0.005 now, "raised at later boundaries".
- Counterparty: discount when fills vs miners > 4× fills vs background (ours ≈ 95% background → n/a).

→ **Making and skill are deliberately separated.** Making pays short-horizon NON-directional liquidity (width-priced); skill pays directional trading. Our lean fills are directional by construction and are meant to score ≈ 0 at 20 s. Every attempt to make the LEAN fills score as making (T1, delayed entry, …) fights the design.

**Fundamental-cycle check** (speed/fundphase.py, END = 44,439, 60 sim min): R/C by seconds since the fund update.

| uid | 0–9 s | 10–19 s | 20–25 s | 26 s+ | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 113 | −0.22 | −0.05 | +0.02 | +0.07 | late fills with the next update AGAINST: −1.19 (16% of $) |
| 252 | +0.59 | +0.49 | +0.43 | +0.80 | 75% of $ in 0–9 s |
| 210 | +0.72 | +0.35 | +0.50 | +0.53 | — |

- → Phase gating is not the main lever (we trail by ≈ 0.5–0.8 in every phase). Consistent with "directional fills, by design".

**Design-consistent fix = a separate NON-directional making layer** whose own fills carry positive R and enough C to lift the miner-wide quality ΣR/ΣC, while the lean engine keeps earning skill.
- Evidence: 3+ ticks-back fills hold value (113 +0.47, 252 +0.98; ALGO sweeps are uninformed and revert within ≈ 60 s).
- Earlier two-sided tries were too close (M5 gate 2; A2/B 5 back at 0.2) or too small (Option A 0.1).

**T5 redesigned and moved up to right after T2:** "deep two-sided sweep ladder" via existing live knobs: mk_rest_none 0, mk_gate_rest 6, mk_rest_frac 0.5, mk_rest_lean_none 0 (both sides on lean books too). Census first; ABAB vs the T2 winner; no restart. Then T3 hold, T4 traffic/size.

## §1852 — 6:25 AM CT — Phase 1b: the 20-s model separates 252's fills cleanly but INVERTS on our strongest lean fills; Phase 2 redesigned

- **Brief:** 101 $73/mo ($2.43/d), net α 1,346, captured 87.8, realized 0; 252 $247/mo. T3 A2: 101 +17.8 / +15.0 / +20.8 vs 252 −2.9 / +8.2 / +10.3.
- The 113 run (END 44,439) returned nothing: the daily tape rotation (09:07 UTC) had already dropped 11-20's data. Lesson: snapshot the tape before the rotation when an analysis needs older windows.
- **101's $300 maker fills** (last 60 sim min), grouped by the model's 20-s prediction in the fill's favour:

| prediction for the fill | 101: share of $ / C / R/C | 252: share of $ / C / R/C |
|---|---|---|
| ADVERSE < −0.5 bp | 15% / +0.38 / −0.10 | 5% / — / **−0.64** |
| adverse −0.5…−0.2 | 14% / +0.47 / +0.18 | 12% / — / −0.03 |
| neutral | 27% / +0.36 / +0.15 | 30% / — / −0.07 |
| fav 0.2…0.5 | 22% / +0.26 / **+0.30** | 28% / — / +0.21 |
| FAV > 0.5 bp | 21% / **+0.06** / **−1.86** | 25% / +0.29 / **+0.57** |
| ALL | R/C +0.04 | R/C +0.26 |

- Counterfactual without the adverse groups: 101 R/C +0.03 (no gain); 252 +0.30.
- **Reading:**
  - For 252 the model sorts fills as intended.
  - For 101 the worst fills are those where the model STRONGLY AGREES with the fill side: our lean step-ins when a move looks most certain. A resting order on the side the price is expected to move toward fills mainly when the prediction FAILS (conditional adverse selection), so it captures ≈ 0.
  - 252's fills come from regular flow, not from failed predictions.
- **Phase 2 redesign:**
  - (a) When the 20-s prediction strongly favours the lean side (fav > ≈ 0.5 bp), step that lean order BACK 1–2 ticks instead of at/inside the touch.
  - (b) A small two-sided layer that quotes only when the model is neutral (|pred| < ≈ 0.2 bp), where our fills already hold value and are balanced.
  - Needs the model live in the agent (features from the state: book top-5, recent prints, fund) → a build + equiv/test_pace + census, then ABAB on 101 after T3.

## §1861 — 8:35 AM CT — Fix 1 "join, don't lead" built (mk_join300) + the user's staggering idea checked against the scorer

**User idea:** stagger in time — lean (skill) quotes, then 20-s (making) quotes, alternating — so lean fills stop hurting making.
- **Scorer check** (repo067 debeta.markout_quality): quality = clamp(ΣR/ΣC, 0, 1) per uid, summed over **every maker fill on every book** in the window. Taker legs are excluded.
- So fills from both phases land in the same ratio, and staggering in time does not separate them. It would roughly halve the lean's skill and still leave the lean fills' −R in the making ratio.
- Real separators: (a) a separate miner (one lean/skill, one pure making); (b) doing the lean as taker legs, which the scorer excludes from making. Option (b) is ruled out on maker miners by the user (11-13/11-16).
- The kept part of the idea: the lean orders should not be the ones sitting alone at the front (§1860 bucket 1). Fix 1 does exactly that.

**Fix 1 = mk_join300** (agents 3ee9e1d9, staged as agents/QuoteAgent.py.next-3ee9e1d9; live is still 75966cb2):
- On $300 vol+calm books (not low), each wanted side is clamped to the OTHERS' best (our own size removed). So we never improve the price alone, and never stay as the sole best after others cancel.
- Logs `JOIN300: n of m sides clamped` once per sim minute. Default 0 = unchanged behaviour.
- Test: speed/abab_join101.sh. Env G = gate setting for both arms (from the gate verdict). 600-s warm-up, then A/B/A/B. Each block end runs pairfills (30 sim min) + fillvalue.
- Deploy and start are scheduled right after the gate verdict (≈ 11:58 AM).

- **Queue check** (since sim 57,995): 130 of 181 (72%) of our $300 fills had the taker continue at the same price (others behind us in the queue) or deeper.

- **$300 offline bound:** doubling the wide-spread $300 size ≈ doubles $300 capture at ≈ the same quality → $300 making credit ≈ 2×.
  - Unknowns for the live test: skill (bigger inventory swings; max_inv 0.3 may bind and skew quotes) and the pace budget (fine: ≈ $68–77k of $450k per book per day).
- **$30: NO.** Continued-taker fills at best lose in every own-share bucket; more at-best size = more losses. (Also matches the failed $30 ladder test, §1880.)
- Size knobs are at their bounds (mk_vol_size 0.1 = max, mk_calm_size 0.12 = max). Staged agents with bounds raised to 0.3 / 0.36 (agents/QuoteAgent.py.next-f1bcce6e; otherwise = 6ca6f5e2). Needs a restart → not during the running $30 imbalance ABAB.
